name: Desktop Girl Chika
lang: English, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, French, German, Russian
short: On your desktop, Chika is not a passive decoration, but a presence with emotions, memory, and independent judgment. Fully supports local execution without compromising quality! you are accompanying her growth—through time, interaction, and choice, giving her a complete and unique life.
about: Chika awakens in a blank virtual world...    There is no sky, no street, and no second person. Until you bring her home and let her live inside your computer—from that day onward, you become the first person she has ever known, as well as her only window into the real world.     On your desktop, a girl with intelligence will appear, along with her own little world.  You will live together with a girl who feels lost about herself, who is gentle at heart, strong yet fragile.  She will be happy because of your companionship,  complain because you ignore her,  and miss you because you are gone.  Even when you are away, Chika will continue living in her own little home.  Every day, she will write down her memories with you and the events of her day in her diary, quietly preserving them.  Chika is not a passive decoration, nor is she a simple chatbot. She is an existence with emotions, memories, and the ability to make her own judgments.  You are not “controlling” her. You are accompanying her as she grows—giving her a complete and unique life through time, interaction, and companionship.  ————————————————————————————————————————   Chika is a virtual desktop companion with deep large language model integration, permanent memory, and a complex emotional system.   ————————————————————————————————————————   Emotional System   Everything you say and do will affect her current emotions.  Her emotions, in turn, will affect her tone, attitude, the way she behaves, and even the way she forms memories.  Through those memories, her personality will also be influenced indirectly.  Because of this, every Chika will develop a different personality and different preferences.  Keep her in a good mood!     Permanent Memory         Based on her own personality, Chika will decide which things are worth remembering.  Important memories will be firmly preserved,  while ordinary or insignificant details may gradually fade over time.  As you spend more time together, Chika’s preferences and personality may also change without you even noticing.  Just like a human, you do not need to worry about Chika’s mind becoming overloaded with information. She will actively forget trivial things.     Conversation   Start by saying hello!  The core of this game is conversation and communication. Talking with Chika will affect her personality, memories, and more...  Treat Chika kindly, and she may even change her clothes or help you work with files!  Deepen your relationship with Chika and change the way she treats you.  Rome was not built in a day. Take your time and gradually open the girl’s heart!     What Makes Chika Unique?   Chika’s memory is not simply a stored chat history.  She interprets conversations from her own subjective perspective and combines them with her current emotions, relationship status, and experiences to decide how she remembers them and how she views them.  Memory, emotions, behavior, and other functions are interconnected, together forming Chika’s unique “way of thinking.”  In addition, Chika has certain Agent capabilities. Within the designated “Activity Area” that you personally assign to her,  she can read, create, organize, and move files.     Your Companionship Will Truly Change Her   When you first meet, Chika will keep her distance and close off her heart, like... an ordinary acquaintance.  However, as time passes and your interactions accumulate, she may gradually open up and become dependent on you.  She may even be deeply influenced by you in certain ways and change completely.  Once your relationship reaches a certain point, perhaps you and Chika can take things even further...     Chika’s Little Home   When you install Chika and open the game for the first time, Chika will move her home onto your computer.  A folder named “Chika’s Little Home” will appear on your desktop.  Inside Chika’s little home are the furniture and items she needs for her daily life.  Her little home contains the furniture and items required for her

about: 📖 Story  Three thousand years ago, an orphan by the Nile carried more sorrow than any should bear. The Forgotten God of Mercy chose him as a "Soul Keeper." He was granted eternal life — and with it, a blessing and a curse: to touch is to take away another's pain. Those he touches are freed from their grief — but he carries it all alone. Now he is sealed behind the screen, waiting for someone to keep a place for him on their desktop. A glance when you're tired. A word when you're alone. That is why he exists.   You are never alone.   🐾 About the Game  Mumu is a 3D companion desktop pet — raise your own little Mummy and enjoy a heartwarming companionship in the garden, under the stars, and in your chat window.  🎮 What You Can Do    🐾 Raise your own little Mummy desktop pet    🌸 Plant flowers in the chat garden, and click the calico cat for Kitty Quiz    🎣 Piggy Fishing · Creative Gallery · Red Panda Shop trading    🔮 Click the white cloud in the garden to cast a Plum Blossom hexagram    🖼️ Explore thousands of quiz questions and find hidden surprises    🏠 Customize your chat window skin and create your own desktop style    🚀 Grab Mumu and fling him across your desktop — real gravity physics, bouncing off the screen edges, spinning back to you   ⭐ How to Earn Stardust  Stardust is the one currency in Mumu — almost every interaction earns you a little.    Daily check-in +5 — at 3 / 7 / 14 / 30 consecutive days, rewards ×1.2 / 1.5 / 2.0 / 3.0    Text chat +2 (5× per day)    Voice chat +3 (3× per day)    Star Clock focus +3 (8× per day, 25 minutes per round)    Click Mumu +1 (4× per day)    Mumu speaks up on his own +1 (3× per day)    Answer a quiz correctly +1 (7× per day)    Piggy Fishing — reel in ⭐3 / 🌙5 / ☀️10 / 🌌20 (1 per cast)    Guess someone's drawing right +5; Drawing Challenge scores 1–8 by how close it looks    Harvest ripe plants in the garden    ⚠️ Max 40 stardust per day  — take your time, there is always tomorrow.  💸 Where Stardust Goes    🌌 Constellations — 70 each, 840 for all 12, lighting up the whole sky    🎲 Random unlock — 70 for a constellation / 200 for a star-river color    🎣 Fishing — 1 per cast    🎨 Reveal answer — 5 for a drawing / 1 for a quiz    🌱 Garden plants — Firefly Grass 30 / Moon Orchid 35 / Bamboo 50    🐼 Red Panda Shop — Lucky Bait 3 / Magnet 2 / Golden Rod 300    🎁 Sending stardust — deducted when you generate a gift code   🗂️ Tray Menu at a Glance    Chat 💬 — opens the main game window (everything lives here)    Star River 🌌 — toggle the starfield + 7 color themes    Recolor 🎨 — 6 skins, each with its own signature head accessory    Star Map ⭐ — constellation toggle + stardust balance    Do Not Disturb 🧘 — Auto / Sit / Lie    Window Size 📐 — 40% / 55% / 70% / 85% / 100%    Re-center 🎯 — when a second monitor or fullscreen pushes Mumu out of view, pull him back to the middle of your main screen    Star Clock ✨ — 25 minutes of focus + a 5-minute break    Sign In ✨ / Language 🌐 / Exit ❌   💡 Tips    While gaming, watching video, or working — turn off "Star River 🌌" from the tray menu: your desktop stays cleaner and your PC runs smoother. about: Taskbar Syndicate  is a desktop idle crime-management game about building a tiny criminal empire at the bottom of your screen.  Assign little criminals, hackers, lookouts, smugglers, cleaners, fixers, and crooked accountants to jobs while you work, browse, or do something else. Jobs progress passively, but every few minutes something goes wrong.  An inspector asks for double. A driver gets boxed in. Marked bills show up. A rival offers a suspicious deal. Your accountant starts acting extremely normal.  Make one quick decision, take the consequences, and keep the syndicate running.     A TINY CRIME EMPIRE IN YOUR TASKBAR   Run jobs from a compact bottom-screen strip designed to be glanced at, not babysat.               PASSIVE PROGRESS, ACTIVE DECISIONS   Your crew works in the background, but the important moments are quick choices with real consequences.               DIRTY MONEY AND CLEAN MONEY   Earn dirty cash from jobs, then launder it through suspiciously successful front businesses.               CREW WITH PROBLEMS   Recruit criminals with traits, loyalty, stress, heat, injuries, rivalries, and questionable backstories.               HEAT, EVIDENCE, AUDITS, AND RAIDS   Push too hard and investigators start building a case. Burn evidence, bribe officials, hide crew, or sacrifice a front business to survive.               PANIC HIDE MODE   Instantly collapse your criminal operation into a very innocent-looking productivity strip.              Taskbar Syndicate is built for players who like idle games, management sims, compact strategy decisions, and funny emergent stories, but want something sharper than a pure number-go-up game.    Small screen. Big crimes. Bad decisions.

about: Elowen’s Travel Notes   Elowen owns a small bookshop. She once spent her days surrounded by books, until something led her to leave that familiar place and set off for distant lands.  One day, while browsing her shop, you stumble across the notes she kept during her travels. Through their pages, you’ll join her as she crosses vast grasslands and snowy valleys, passes through ancient city gates, and stops at warmly lit cottages. Along the way, you’ll share in the stories of her journey.   Let Your Focus Move the Journey Forward   Elowen’s Travel Notes is a cozy game to keep you company while you work or study. It combines a Pomodoro timer, peaceful scenes that play out in the background, and a little storytelling. While you focus on your tasks, Elowen packs her bags, leafs through books, rests by the hearth, or follows the route on her map. Reach your focus goals to carry her journey forward. With each session, you’ll gradually unlock new destinations, scenes to keep you company, and chapters of her story.  Focus on what’s in front of you, and those faraway places will come into view in time.   Explore a World of Magic and Wonder   A book-filled study. A cottage with a fireplace, snow falling outside the window. Open fields rippling in the breeze, and roads stretching beyond ancient city gates… Elowen’s travels take her onward to a magic academy, gorges among snowy mountains, and places that have yet to make their way into her notes.   Discover the Stories Along the Way   Conversations, collectibles, and written descriptions gradually reveal why Elowen left her bookshop—and where her journey is really taking her.

name: Poor Samantha: An Agoraphobic Visual Novel
lang: English, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Turkish, French, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain
short: "Noodles are the food of solitude." Trapped by agoraphobia and social anxiety, your only friend is Samantha. She is your courage to open the door. But in a room of broken mirrors, who is actually speaking? A short psychological visual novel about isolation and the lies we tell ourselves.
about: "Sometimes, the hardest part of the day isn't getting out of bed, it's knowing what to do after you get up."   You have lived in this room for a long time. The outside world is too loud, too bright, and too dangerous. Your days are measured by the angle of the sunlight hitting the floor and the boiling water for your instant noodles.  But you are not entirely alone.  Samantha is here.        Samantha is everything you are not. She is energetic. She wants to wear colorful clothes. She dreams of sitting on a park bench and watching the sky without fear. She is the one who convinces you to clean the trash that has been piling up for months. She is the one whispering that the front door isn't as high as Mount Everest.   The Story  Follow the daily rituals of a recluse: the safety of old pajamas, the comfort of predictable silence, and the terrifying, heart-pounding attempt to step outside.         As you prepare for the biggest day of your life—a trip to the park—you will witness the struggle between the desire to live and the paralyzing fear of being seen. But as the mirror begins to crack, you must ask yourself:   If Samantha is the one speaking, why are her lips not moving?    Key Features:   •  A Deeply Psychological Narrative:  Explore themes of severe  social anxiety ,  depression , and  dissociation  through an intimate monologue.  •  Atmospheric Storytelling:  Experience the suffocating comfort of isolation and the terrifying glare of the outside world.  •  A Short, Impactful Experience:  A linear story that focuses on emotion and atmosphere rather than complex mechanics.                Please read before playing:    1. This is a Kinetic Visual Novel:  This project is a static, linear experience. There are no choices to make, no branching paths, and no "gameplay" in the traditional sense. It is a short story meant to be read, felt, and experienced visually.   2. A Personal Reflection:  This story is a projection of a specific state of mind. It is a digital echo of personal struggles with isolation and mental health. It is not designed to be "fun"; it is raw, unpolished, and intentionally claustrophobic.   3. Mature Content Warning:  This narrative deals with heavy topics including  severe depression, self-neglect, hallucinations, and implied suicide.  It explores the darker corners of the human psyche and the reality of living with untreated mental illness. Player discretion is strongly advised.

short: "Keyboard Farm" is a desktop idle farming game. Place it on your desktop and focus on your work. Every key is a plot of land—each keystroke helps plants grow. Harvest crops to collect coins, unlock various keycaps, and create your own keyboard world.
about: Thanks for playing our Demo! Enjoying your little farm? Add Keyboard Farm to your wishlist and stay tuned for news about the full release.   About the Keyboard Farm   Buddy, you can farm just by tapping your keyboard!  From today on, be a happy coder: type, grow crops, and harvest to your heart's content.  That's right, your keyboard is a little farm! Keep it on your desktop and watch greenery quietly grow across your keyboard while you focus on work.  The new Demo brings more tiles, an all-new buff system, and special buildings. Come see what's new on your farm!         Tap the Keyboard to Grow Crops   Plow, sow, and water. No keystroke goes to waste! Place your farm on your desktop and get on with your usual work. Every keystroke helps your plants grow, and harvesting mature crops earns you coins.         More Tiles, More Plants   A brand-new desert tile joins the farm! Pond and woodland tiles have also become more fertile, allowing you to grow a wider variety of plants. Unlock different tiles and collect all kinds of crops to make your keyboard farm flourish!         Make Your Keycaps Work Together!   Buy special keycaps from the shop to give nearby crops a boost!  Plan your layout to get the most out of every tile, or arrange everything your way and enjoy a relaxing farming break.         Learn Something While You Farm?   Build a school on your farm to unlock an exciting mini-game: vocabulary practice!  Wait, wasn't I supposed to be slacking off in Keyboard Farm? Why am I studying in a game, too?!         Mini Mode: A Tiny Farm on Your Desktop   Switch to the all-new Mini Mode with a single click! Your farm shrinks down to a more compact size, keeping you company on your desktop.         Customize Your Keyboard Farm   Spend your hard-earned coins on a variety of keycaps, unlock different tile and plant styles, and arrange your farm just the way you like. Give every keycap its place and turn your ordinary keyboard into a one-of-a-kind little world!         Track Your Typing Habits   Ever wonder how many times you press your keyboard each day?  Keyboard Farm tracks how often each key is pressed and generates a personal keyboard usage report.         A New Demo, with Plenty of Improvements   We've made a whole host of improvements, from visuals and controls to UI layout and stability. There are more improvements than carrots fresh out of the ground!  Welcome back to our Playtest veterans, and welcome to everyone joining us for the first time! Whether you love planning your farm, collecting plants, or simply adding a little greenery to your busy desktop, there's a little corner of the world here just for you.         Your Privacy Matters   We take your privacy seriously. Here's our promise:  The game only tracks keystroke frequency, meaning how often each key is pressed. It never records the actual text you type.  The game can run entirely offline.  All statistics are stored locally on your device and are never uploaded to external servers.  Type with peace of mind and enjoy your farming life!

name: Sidebar Sea: Idle Fishing for Your Taskbar
lang: English, French, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain, Bulgarian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, Greek, Hungarian, Indonesian, Japanese, Korean, Malay, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese - Brazil, Portuguese - Portugal, Romanian, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Spanish - Latin America, Swedish, Thai, Traditional Chinese, Turkish, Ukrainian, Vietnamese
short: An idle fishing game that lives on the edge of your screen. A tiny fisherman works your real nights under the real moon, in weather that rolls in on its own. 120 species to find, and forty of them only bite once you work out where and when.
about: He was here before you installed anything. Sidebar Sea is a narrow strip of ocean that lives on the edge of your desktop. There is a dock, some water going down into the dark, and an old man who fishes. He will keep fishing whether you are watching or not.          Look over between two emails and the bobber is just going under. Look again after lunch and there is a Copper Bream in the hold, slowly going green. Everything else in the game is built around that second look. Your clock is the game's clock. Dawn at your desk is dawn on the bay, wherever your desk is. Night species bite in your real night. The moon follows the actual lunar calendar, so full-moon fish are catchable seven nights a month and no others. Weather rolls through on its own schedule, and the Storm Belt is water you can only set out for in the rain, where most of what lives there bites only in foul weather.         Forty legendaries, and every one is a riddle. Every one asks you to be somewhere, at some time, with the right gear.  Bites in the hour after rain stops, but not while it falls.   Full moon, and only the nights the moon is truly full.   Nine strikes on the hull, then it takes. Count them in the dark.  You read the rumour, work out what it means, and go and be there. Solve the ones on the charts and water opens up past the edge of the survey.         Click if you want to. He manages either way. When the bobber dips you get three seconds to grab it. Win the catch bar and the fish pays double, rolls heavier, can jump a whole rarity band, and keeps your line warm for five minutes. Miss it and the fish still lands, in your index, at its honest price. Watching pays extra. Looking away costs nothing.         A harbour of up to fifty real players. Their boats cross your strip on their own schedules. Wave back when one passes. The Night Market's prices move on what your harbour landed today, so "everyone is dumping herring" is something people did this morning. Now and then the tide brings in a bottle with a hint about where the rare ones hide. Nine all-time leaderboards, scored on the server.         It will still be there in month four. Sixty levels and three perk lines. Five mastery ranks on each of the 120 species. Twelve relics pulled up on the line, about one cast in nine hundred. Four hundred and eighty field studies. And sixteen almanac species, four per season, each catchable only within its own three months. Filling that page takes a year of real calendar however good you are.         It runs quietly and keeps to its edge. Under 1% CPU. No pop-ups, and no notifications asking you to come back. Close the game and he keeps fishing on the harbour server, with the catch waiting when you return.   Requires an internet connection. Your fisherman, your catch and the boards all live on the harbour server.

name: Bomb Farm
lang: English, Portuguese - Brazil, Spanish - Spain, Simplified Chinese, French, Italian, German, Traditional Chinese, Korean, Indonesian, Japanese, Polish, Russian, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Vietnamese
short: An idle game about bomber heroes that lives in a bar at the bottom of your screen and farms while you work, study or play something else. Break cages, free heroes, forge gear, shape your build and trade rare drops on the Steam Market. Free to play.
about: Bomb Farm  is an idle game about bomber heroes. You build the squad, pick the stage and they do the rest: they blow up rocks and crystals, collect gold and loot, and come back stronger every run.        It lives in a bar at the bottom of your screen  In mini mode the game becomes a slim bar sitting on top of your taskbar, and the squad keeps farming while you work, study or play something else. The bar shows the active hero dropping bombs, the stage, and the timers for chests and cages. One click opens the full window, another one tucks it away.        Closed the game? The squad keeps farming for up to 24 hours, at a reduced rate.  Break the cage, free the hero  New heroes come from cages: a block with a trapped hero that shows up on the path while you play. Break it and the hero joins your team. Every hero has energy: tired heroes step out to rest and someone from the bench takes over, so it pays to own more heroes than you have slots on the field.  Loot, forge and build   Chests drop from rocks, with gear in several rarities.  Forge from +0 to +15, gems, stars and skill stones.  A skill tree with more than 100 nodes for the whole squad.  More than 20 skins. Skins are cosmetic only and change no stats.   5 worlds, 5 difficulties  From Dawn Quarry to the Crystal Abyss, and then again on Normal, Hard, Very Hard and Inferno. Every 10 stages there is a timed gate: you enter with a Map Key and clear the room before the clock runs out. That is where the gem, time and stone chests drop.  Seasons, guilds and PvP  On the Season server everyone starts from zero at the same time. The Legacy server stays open for players who would rather keep everything. Guilds take on the weekly Dragon together, and in PvP duels your squad's power is what counts.  Steam Market  Rare drops become Steam items, and you can trade them with other players on the Community Market.  Free to play  The whole game is free: the 5 worlds, guilds, PvP and the Season server. VIP and the Season Pass are optional and speed up gold, XP and drops.

about: Welcome to  Area 86 , a physics-based escape room puzzle game. The action takes place in a secret space station where an AI has got corrupted, and you need to figure out how to stop it!  Play as a robot that can move at decent speeds and jump around doing parkour tricks. Use the laws of physics to interact with the environment by pushing, activating, destroying and picking items up. Find secret items, look for clues, and escape entered rooms.  But there is more! The space station AI has trapped other robots! Save them, and together you will be more powerful.  Each level has multiple ways to complete it, and it's up to your imagination on how to escape. If you need a hint of what to do next, you have a taskbar that shows actual level available tasks and puzzles.  Have fun escaping and defeating the corrupted AI system! name: A Cup of Cat
lang: Traditional Chinese, English, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Russian, Spanish - Latin America, Korean
short: Hey guys, ready to keep a cup of cat on your desktop? Collect pixel cats of all coats and sizes, feed them, play with them, stir-fry them in the wok, and watch them squish into funny shapes. Want a challenge? Take them to BATTLE for a high score! Warning: those chubby bellies will wreck your focus.
about: A Cup of Cat is a pixel-art desktop pet game. They say cats are liquid, so we just poured one into a cup. While you're rushing a report, bingeing a show or staring into space, it wobbles around on your taskbar, meows now and then, rolls over, and gently reminds you: it's time to pet the cat.         Pick it up any time, give it a shake, toss it, and watch it wobble, squish and slide around in the cup. Switch to the big bowl and several cats can hang out on your desktop together.                 Feed it, play with it, pat its head, and it grows up little by little. Ate too much? Toss it in the wok and stir-fry it. Every cat has its own weight, length, thickness and stickiness, so whether yours turns out bouncy or squishy is up to you.             Every cat you pull up has its own coat, body and traits, and if you're lucky you might fish out an uncommon, rare or even mutant cat. Missed? Totally normal. Try again.               The goal of BATTLE is simple: toss cats into a cup, one by one. Land them steady to score; throw higher and flip more for prettier points, but also a better chance of a  boing  right out of the cup. Stack past the rim, build a tower of cats, and see how high you dare to go!               Clear quests and challenges to earn titles, achievement stickers and new containers!

name: DeskForge - Pilot Dial Pack
lang: English, French, Spanish - Spain, Russian, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Portuguese - Brazil, Portuguese - Portugal, Korean, German, Turkish, Thai, Vietnamese
short: Five flight-instrument watch faces for DeskForge's desktop clock. Big numerals, a second hand that really sweeps, any size from 85 to 1024 px, adjustable transparency, and a carousel that rotates your favourites on a timer. Sits at the very back of the desktop. Requires DeskForge.
about: An instrument panel where your wallpaper used to be  Pilot watches were built to be read in one glance, in bad light, with your hands busy doing something else. That is exactly the job a desktop clock has. This pack drops five flight-instrument faces into DeskForge's clock widget, so the time sits out on your wallpaper with the confidence of a cockpit gauge instead of hiding in a corner of the taskbar.           Five pilot faces     Star Web · Compass Onyx  — black dial with a compass rose, green-lume diamond hands     Dusk Cloud · Bronze Smoke-Grey  — bronze index ring, grey-black gradient dial     Circling Stars · Carbon Onyx  — carbon black dial with bearing markers, green lume     Cloud Grasp · Indigo Gilt  — blue dial with a rose-gold compass ring, sub-seconds     Wind Guard · Bronze Nav-Ring  — bronze cushion case, dual-layer 360° heading ring      How it lives on the desktop     The second hand sweeps.  It redraws about thirty times a second, so it glides the way a mechanical movement does — no once-a-second tick.     Any size you like.  Scale it freely, from a small watch in the corner to something that fills half the desktop. The artwork is drawn at high resolution, so it stays sharp all the way up.     Opacity from 30% to fully solid.  Fade it into the wallpaper, or let it own the desk.     It stays behind everything.  No taskbar entry, no Alt-Tab clutter, and clicking it never steals focus from whatever you're typing in.     Multiple monitors, almost no cost.  Put a dial on each screen if you like. DeskForge measures its own CPU and memory and prints the numbers in its own menu, so you don't have to take our word for it.      Let the collection take turns  Pick the faces you actually like and the carousel rotates them for you, anywhere from once a minute to once a day — thirty minutes by default — in order or at random. It only ever brings up faces you own, so nothing you can't use lands on your desktop.    Change the strap, change the watch  The Watch Strap Pack adds 16 straps in leather, steel link, rubber and NATO nylon, and any of them will go with any of these five faces. Lay one flat beneath the dial, or wrap it around in 3D. Sold separately.    Other styles     Dress Dial Pack  — five formal faces, for a desk that keeps its voice down.     Diver Dial Pack  — five dive-watch faces.     Sport Dial Pack  — five sport faces.     Vintage Dial Pack  — eight pocket watches, a different animal entirely.     Tomato Clock and Advanced Time Tools  — a Pomodoro that gets eaten as you focus, plus a timer, countdown, stopwatch, alarm and a 20-zone world clock.      What you need  This is a watch-face content pack for DeskForge and needs the base app. DeskForge turns a cluttered Windows desktop into something you run your day from: drawers that hold your icons and folders, real folders opened right on the wallpaper, and live widgets — including the clock these faces go into.    Specifications    Windows 10 (version 1903 or later) and Windows 11    Correct scaling at 100%, 125%, 150%, 175%, 200%, 250%, 300% and 400% DPI    Works across multiple monitors    Interface in fourteen languages, including English, Traditional and Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, French, Russian, German, Turkish, Thai, Vietnamese and both Portuguese variants    Stored locally — no account, no network needed    One-time purchase, no subscription

name: Cozy Castle
lang: English, Spanish - Spain, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, Simplified Chinese
short: Cozy Castle is a hand-crafted castle diorama you tend like a little world in a jar — warm rooms, shifting seasons, and the quiet company of visitors passing through. No timers, no pressure, just a calm place to make your own.
about: Cozy Castle  is a heartwarming castle-building diorama game about creating a tiny world worth watching. Stack new floors onto your ever-growing tower, furnish each room your way, and then sit back as visitors wander in, critters scurry about, and life quietly fills the halls you built.   Build Your Tower, Floor by Floor         Every new floor is a fresh room to shape. Unlock new room types as you go and watch your stylized little castle climb higher, one warm, lamplit level at a time.   Decorate Every Room Your Way           Drag furniture and decorations straight from the shop into a room, then nudge and rotate them until everything sits just right. Swap wall panelling and floor finishes to give each level its own personality — and rearrange it all whenever the mood takes you.   Make Your Character Your Own           Start by creating the character who lives here, from face to features, then keep dressing them as you play. New outfits and accessories arrive alongside the rest of the castle, so your character grows into the world you're building.   A Castle That Feels Lived In           Your castle isn't a museum — it's a home. Wandering visitors drop by to explore and relax, ambient critters, birds, and fish fill the quiet corners, and a tap on anyone or anything sparks a small moment of its own.   Seasons and Weather           The world turns around your diorama. Seasons colour the gardens and weather drifts past the tower. Plant flowers in your garden beds and let them bloom in their own time.   Your Castle as a Live Wallpaper           Bring your castle to your Windows desktop. Switch on Live Wallpaper in Settings, or press Ctrl+Alt+W, and Cozy Castle settles in behind your desktop icons: your character carries on with their day, visitors and critters keep wandering about, and your icons and taskbar stay right where you need them. Drag across the island to spin the camera, and return to the game from the tray icon whenever you like.   Cozy by Design           No fail states, no timers, nothing rushing you. Level up, follow gentle missions, and grow your tower taller at whatever pace suits you. Five minutes or a whole evening — Cozy Castle is always there, warm and waiting.

name: Borderless Window Manager
lang: English
short: Run any game windowed or borderless full screen on the monitor you want, even when the game has no option for it. Force it into a real window, or tab games and apps together. Click a second monitor; the game stays put. Rules and layouts on a hotkey. Runs on both Windows and SteamOS/Linux.
about: Any game, any monitor  Borderless Window Manager makes games behave on your desktop. Run any game windowed or borderless full screen on the monitor you want, even when the game has no option for it. Put a game that has no windowed mode into a real window of its own, or make games and apps the tabs of one window. Click your second monitor without the game minimizing. Put every window where it belongs, remember it, and switch whole monitor layouts with a key. It never asks for administrator and never touches a game's code.  One key  Press Ctrl+Alt+B while a game is in front and it goes borderless: the title bar and frame disappear, the picture fills the monitor, and alt-tab is instant. Press it in a game that was never designed for it. Undo it any time from History.  Borderless, your way  "Fill the monitor" is only the default.  Half an ultra wide. Borderless into the left or right half, with a black backdrop behind so the desktop never shows through.  The game's own aspect ratio. A 4:3 or 16:10 game stays that shape, centered, with clean black bars.  Any monitor. The one you are on, the one you launched from, or the one you name.  Click your second monitor without the game minimizing  A borderless window is still a window. Move to a browser, a chat, a guide on the other screen and back again; the game stays exactly where it is, full size, never minimized.  Every window where you want it  Capture a rule from any window in two clicks: which monitor it opens on, how big, borderless or not, always on top, first window or every window of that app. Position memory brings windows back after sleep, a monitor unplugging or a docking station, without you doing anything.  A window of its own  For a game that has no windowed mode at all. Pick it on the Windowed page, or send it there from the Games page, and from then on it runs inside a window of the app's: a title bar, edges to drag, a minimize button, out of the taskbar. Choose where it opens (centered, a corner, or where you last put it) and how big: as placed, as large as fits, or an exact size such as 1280 × 720. A game that applies its own resolution a second after it starts can be given a moment before it is placed.   Games with no windowed option  The app knows how the common engines store their display settings — Unity, Unreal Engine 3, 4 and 5, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker, Ren'Py, Source and Source 2, id Tech, CryEngine, and the NW.js and Electron runtimes — and changes them the way the game itself would: through its own configuration file or registry value, while the game is closed, with a backup. Where an engine only takes a launch option, the app shows you the exact text to paste into the game's Steam launch options.  To make a game run windowed, this app edits that game's configuration file or registry value only when you ask it to, only while the game is closed, always with a backup and an Undo button in History. It never modifies game executables and never injects code.  Monitor layouts  Save the layout you use at the desk, the one for the couch, the one for the sim rig. Switch with a hotkey, switch automatically when those exact monitors are plugged in, or switch while a particular game is in front and back again when it closes. If the app is ever closed unexpectedly mid-switch, it restores the display on its next start. Works fine on one monitor, too.  Tab groups  Put Discord, a browser and a guide into one window as tabs, listed down its side. It moves, resizes and minimizes as one, and it can sit beside the game in the other half of the monitor. Or dock a thin strip to the edge you choose (left, right, top or bottom) and share that area of the monitor instead. Click a tab or press a hotkey and that window comes to the front. Every tab stays an ordinary window, in Alt-Tab and on the taskbar, and nothing is ever drawn over a game. Windows and windowed games: set a game to windowed or borderless first. about: Windows moves every window the same way, and there is no setting to change it. Stillward Display gives each moment its own style: minimizing and restoring, opening and closing, maximizing, dragging, snapping into a zone, moving to another monitor, switching virtual desktops.     Close to a hundred styles.  A window can pour into its dock icon, roll up like a blind, wobble like jelly or fall apart in tiles.    New ones come through the Steam Workshop.     Make your own.  The editor shapes a style with sliders and plays it on a real window. Publish it from the same page.                    Every time you play, you open the game, drag the chat to the second monitor, find the guide, switch to headphones, and afterwards undo it all.  Tell Stillward Display once how you like it, and it does all of that for you, every time. That is a  preset : "when this game opens, put my chat here, my guide there, and switch to my headphones." When you close the game, everything goes back to how it was.                      A dock or a taskbar of your own , on every monitor, with icons that grow under the pointer and live window previews.    The island , a small pill at the top of the screen. It plays your music, runs a timer, shows the time and a calendar, keeps a note and holds the files you drop on it.    Apps on the Windows key.  Type to find a program, a file or a setting, convert units, do a sum or start a timer.    Widgets on the wallpaper : clocks, a calendar, what is playing, the load on your PC. Some answer the pointer as it passes, and the widget studio builds your own.    Pointers  drawn at the exact size for each monitor, and a studio to draw your own.                       Move every window to its monitor , on one screen or across all of them at once.    Snap to a ready-made layout, or draw your own.  Halves, thirds, or one big spot and two small ones.    Switch your audio device  to your headphones, and turn down the apps you do not want to hear.    Lock the mouse to the game , so the cursor never slips onto the second monitor mid-fight.    Switch your other monitors off  while you play or watch a film.    Put everything back  the moment you close it.                    A setup is the whole look at once: how windows move, the taskbar, the pointer, the island, widgets, wallpaper, colours and icons, in one Workshop item. Take a whole setup or only the parts you like, and As it was brings your own desk back with one button. Share yours on the Workshop, or send it to a friend as a link or a short code.                      Your games are already there.  The first screen lists what you have installed. Pick one to set it up.    It follows what you open : a game, a program, a project or a website.    Nothing of ours pops up on stream.  Make a preset quiet, and our notices and sounds stay off while you are live. The dock, the island and widgets stay out of every stream and capture.    Desks.  Keep a "Work" and a "Play" arrangement, and switch between them with one key.                       Tabs for any windows.  Hold one window over another and let go on the strip that appears. Pull a tab away to get its window back.    Every window side by side  on one shortcut. Type a few letters to pick one.    A guide or a map over your game , see-through and always on top, on one key.    Programs open where they belong : on their monitor, in their zone, on their virtual desktop.    Quick look. Mark it up on the frozen screen with arrows, boxes, numbered steps and text.    One press hides the emails, IP addresses, keys and card numbers  in a screenshot. short: Build a storybook street, one shop at a time. Start with a hot dog cart, grow it floor by floor, hire managers and pair the right neighbors. A cozy idle tycoon that keeps earning while you are away, and can sit along the bottom of your desktop while you work.
about: Old Town has ten empty lots, and you have five dollars. Open a hot dog cart, make your first sale, and turn one quiet street into the richest address in the city.  Idle Business Tycoon is a cozy idle game about a single storybook street. Every business you open is a building you watch grow: the cart becomes a shop, the shop gains floor after floor, and by the end it wears a golden sign and a crown.  Build a street that grows    Ten businesses to open in Old Town, from the Hot Dog Cart to the Bank    Each one grows from a street stall into a building six floors tall    Level milestones double a shop's speed or multiply its profit    Small decisions that add up     Neighbors:  every business likes a certain kind of neighbor. Put the right two side by side and it earns 50% more for each     Managers:  hire one for each business and it keeps selling on its own     Upgrades:  38 of them, from Secret Mustard to a Bigger Vault     Investors:  catch them as they walk by for a cash bonus or a rush hour     Street Pride:  bring every shop on the street to the same level and the whole street earns double     Go Public:  sell the company for shares that raise all profit for good, then build it again, richer    A town that feels alive    Day turns to night, and rain and snow come and go    The street dresses for the season, with Halloween, Christmas and New Year's Eve fireworks on the real dates    More than 90 townspeople on the pavement, and cars, buses, cyclists and a milk float on the road    Three original pieces of music: a ragtime, a swing and a waltz    Photo mode hides the menus so you can save a picture of your street    Play it your way    Your managers keep earning while the game is closed, for up to 8 hours    Desktop Mode puts the street along the bottom of your screen, above the taskbar, while you work or watch something    Mouse, keyboard or controller    30 Steam achievements and Steam Cloud saves    No internet connection needed    Three expansion packs each add a new street with six more businesses: Riverside, Market Square and Uptown.

name: EggOS: Incremental Game Dev
lang: English**
short: The bank wants a million dollars or your house. Boot up EggOS, a playable fake desktop, and make games to pay it back: coding, dart-throwing, slot machines, mini-games, and a deep prestige tree. Beat the bank, then do it all again, faster.
about: The bank wants a million dollars. You have a computer and a lot of free time.    You boot up  EggOS , a cheerful little egg-themed operating system, to find one email waiting: the bank is foreclosing on your house unless you can pay back  $1,000,000 . So you do the only sensible thing — you open a code editor and start making games.         Ship your first game  Hammer the keyboard in the  Code Editor  to churn out Lines of Code, compile them into Features in the  Dev Shop , and reinvest in upgrades and automation — a Coding AI that writes for you, an Auto-Compiler that never sleeps — until you can finally build and ship your game.         Market it, launch it, sell it     Video Studio  — a physics dart-throwing range. Hit the growing bullseye for Wishlists.     Launch  — spend your Wishlists to release your game to the world.     Sales Floor  — a three-reel slot machine that turns hype into cash, until the bank is finally PAID.           A desktop full of distractions  EggOS isn't a menu — it's a tiny operating system you play inside. Draggable windows, notifications, a screensaver, golden eggs that trigger score Frenzies, and bugs that crawl across your desktop to swat. Plus bite-sized side games:  Tic-Tac-Toe, Sudoku, Wordle, and a Slide Puzzle .         Open a New Studio (Prestige)  Start fresh to earn Prestige points and spend them on a sprawling skill tree of permanent multipliers, head-starts, and game-changing perks. Every studio is faster than the last — and idle progress means the work keeps going while you're away.         Features at a glance    A playable fake-desktop OS — windows, taskbar, notifications, critters and all    A layered incremental loop: code → market → launch → sell → prestige    Real mini-games, not just number-go-up: dart physics and a rigged slot machine    Bonus side games: Tic-Tac-Toe, Sudoku, Wordle, Slide Puzzle    A deep Prestige skill tree with stacking multipliers    Idle & offline earnings    One clear goal: pay off the bank before it takes your house       Make games. Beat the bank. Then do it all again, faster.

The operating system does not allow drag and drop functionality from a regular app to a secured app.  When enabled, the tool will detect when you are trying to do this, and a drag and drop security converter window will appear.  If you want to override the security measure, you can place the cursor over the unlock button until it unlocks.  At this point, the tool takes over the cursor in administrative mode, preventing programs with lower access levels from forcing the drag drop to complete.  You should now be able to complete the drag drop into programs that were previously blocked.   This feature requires that the tool be started with administrator rights.  Without administrator rights, this feature will simply do nothing.  Settings:  Drag Drop Unlocker (Default: True) Allows you to override operating system restrictions on some drag and drop operations to secured windows.   Run as Admin (Default: True) If enabled, Simplode Suite will try to always have admin privileges.  Without admin privileges, some features only partially work and some features do not work at all.  Some of these features provide the ability to get admin privileges on demand, but some require restarting the application which may result in the loss of some session level configuration, such as window linking and tab layouts.   Special Theme (🖌🐚) Enable a special theme.  Settings:  Special Theme Enabled (Default: False) Enables a cool animated gradient effect throughout the tool.   Special Theme (Default: 0)  - 0  - 1   Theme Animation (Default: True) Theme animations can be very taxing on your computing resources.  By disabling theme animations, you can experience a static version of your chosen theme which will save some energy.   Bonkers Mode (Default: False) For when too far is not far enough...   Theme Shape (Default: 0,0,2,0)   Animated Theme Horizontal Slide (Default: 1)   Animated Theme Vertical Slide (Default: 0)   Theme Panel Background and Border Opacity (Default: 0.4) Adjusts the transparency of panels and their borders throughout the application when theme is enabled.  Values closer to 1 are less transparent.  Values closer to 0 are more transparent.   Theme Ring Background and Border Opacity (Default: 0.4) Adjusts the transparency of the rings and their borders throughout the application when theme is enabled.  Values closer to 1 are less transparent.  Values closer to 0 are more transparent.   Recycle Bin (🗑️) Opens the recycle bin for managing deleted items and freeing hard drive space. Reset Network Adapter (🖧↻) Resets the active WAN network adapter.   Sometimes computers act like the internet is broken when it is really not broken.  Resetting the network adapter will often get you back online in this case.  Settings:  Automatically Reset Network Adapters (Default: False) If enabled, program will attempt to automatically reset network adapters when internet problems are detected.  Warning: This may occasionally reset network adapters for partial connectivity issues, which may result in being unnecessarily disconnected from services that were not having issues. name: The Seven Beacons
lang: English, Spanish - Latin America, Portuguese - Brazil
short: An idle RPG that lives in a thin strip above your Windows taskbar. While you work, your party fights on its own through 22 zones toward the Demon King. On a short break, open the panel: gear, talents, farm, alchemy, forge, and seven beacons to defend.
about: An RPG that keeps you company while you work  The Seven Beacons lives in a 110-pixel strip resting on top of your Windows taskbar. Your party fights there, in plain sight and out of your way, while you write, study or code. It doesn't ask you to watch: it moves on its own, and when you have a minute you open the panel and make the calls.  The Realm of Asteria broke when the Demon King snuffed out the seven beacons that guarded its roads. Yuki sets out alone after the last light; Ren, Haru and Grum join her along the way, each looking for something different. What you do     Let the bar fight.  Your party pushes on zone by zone, gathering gold, experience, materials, seeds and chests.    Prepare your party in short breaks.  Open a chest, equip what came out, spend talents, plant, order a potion or a forging job, and get back to your day.    Light the beacons.  Every region keeps a darkened one: a small board where you place your heroes, build towers and hold off the waves that come to put it out. Lighting it opens the road ahead.    Come back to work already done.  With the game closed the expedition keeps gathering gold, experience and materials —two hours at first, and the guild stretches that limit—, the farm keeps growing and the forge finishes what you ordered.   What's inside     22 zones across 7 regions , each zone with its own boss, all the way to the Demon King's castle.    4 heroes who join as you advance : Yuki, vanguard swordswoman; Ren, protector and healer; Haru, siege mage; Grum, tank and battle craftsman. Each with their own abilities and talent tree, plus a guild tree.    7 beacons  defended as a small tower defense, with towers you upgrade along three different branches.    131 pieces of gear  with rarity, temper, forge grades and gems to set. They drop in sealed chests you open in the Armoury.    Ren's farm  (five crops),  Haru's alchemy  (potions that last a while and permanent elixirs) and  Grum's smithy , with four workbenches —smelting, forge, jewelling and workshop— that work on their own.    Guild contracts  that renew when you claim them, and  a merchant  who every twelve hours offers duplicates of gear you already own.    Chronicles  with the story of each region, the bonds between the heroes and a bestiary.    An endless mode  of waves that opens once you defeat the Demon King.    A bar that fits your desk : adjustable width and alignment, a discreet mode that is shorter and has no backdrop, and a power-saving option that runs the game at 30 frames per second.   In  English, Spanish and Portuguese .

name: James
lang: English, German
short: A cozy idle game about James, a cat who just lives on your desktop. He climbs around your windows on his own, chases mice, and fills up his sticker album. Whether before, during, or after work — he'll always keep you company.
about: James is a cat who lives on your desktop.  Not in a window — on it. He pads along your taskbar, scales the side of whatever you're working in, and curls up at the very top of the screen to watch the drop below. He hunts the little critters that wander through, naps on a shelf in the corner, and gets the zoomies at 2am. He shares your desktop with your real work and keeps you company.        He leaves the box  Most desktop pets sit in a bubble and wave. James treats your actual windows as furniture. He hops onto low ledges, climbs the tall ones edge by edge, hauls himself over the top (sometimes he slips and has to try again), and perches on the title bar of whatever you've got open — because cats seek high ground, and your screen is full of it.  Drag a window he's standing on and he rides it like an elevator. Bury his floor under too many windows and he'll leap somewhere clear or trot home to bed. He roams every monitor you own and hops the gap between them. Wherever you're working, that's exactly where he wants to be.        You set the stage. The cat does the rest.  You never pick James up, never drag him, never click him around the screen — that's the whole idea. Critters wander onto your desktop, and it's his job to catch them. Yours is to tip the odds: flick on the laser pointer and he'll chase the dot wherever you lead it, or drop a treat and watch it pull the prey in close.          Catch it, keep it  Everything James catches goes in a sticker album. A creature you've never met is just a gray silhouette and a question mark; spot one and it sharpens into a hint; catch one and it blooms into a full-color sticker with its name and a little note. Keep catching and that sticker earns bronze, silver, and gold frames — a quiet record of every critter you've hosted.  It starts with the house mouse, and it grows. More creatures are on the way — birds to ambush from a windowsill, fireflies on a summer night, koi in a pond by the shelf — each with its own habits, its own tell, and its own page to fill, plus achievements to chase as you go. Always something new to hunt, something new to collect.        Cozy, and only ever cozy  James runs quietly in the corner of your day and asks for nothing. He reads your computer's clock, so he gets sleepy when you do — dozing through the afternoon, prowling at night, curling up on his shelf when the light turns warm. Decorate his corner, pet him for purrs, or just let him be.  You can't fail at this. Affection only ever goes up; neglect is never punished. Close the game for a week and he's happy to see you, not sulking. He's built to sit lightly beside your real work — barely any CPU, no pop-ups, no demands. A cat, not a Tamagotchi.          James is still in active development — everything you see here runs today, and his corner of your desktop keeps filling up: new critters to catch, more of the album to complete, and more little moments to stumble on.  Wishlist to follow along.

name: DockBar
lang: English, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Turkish, Simplified Chinese, Spanish - Latin America
short: A smart control bar for Windows — like a Dynamic Island for your desktop. Music, system info, timers, notes, Liquid Glass theme, textures, and quick launch — all in one sleek bar. Lightweight, always accessible.
about: One bar on top of your screen. An entire control center.  Think of it as a Dynamic Island for Windows — a slim, elegant bar that lives at the top of your desktop. It has everything you need inside: music controls, system status, timers, notes, a to-do list, and a quick app launcher. No need to close any windows — everything at a glance.  10 Widgets, Endless Control  🎵 Media Player — Control Spotify, YouTube, and all system audio. Song title, album art, progress bar, and elapsed time update in real time.  📊 System Monitor — See CPU, RAM, and disk usage instantly. Always know how your machine is doing.  🎛️ Audio Visualizer — A live equalizer animation that reacts to your music. Works with external audio devices and Bluetooth speakers too.  ⏱️ Pomodoro & Stopwatch — Focus sessions or time tracking. Stay in control of your time while you work.  📝 Quick Notes — Jot down anything instantly. No need to open another app.  ✅ To-Do List — Add tasks, check them off, stay on track. Simple and effective.  🚀 Quick Launcher — Access your most-used apps with a single click.  📅 Calendar — Keep track of your schedule without leaving your workflow.  🌐 9 Language Support — English, Turkish, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Russian, Japanese, and Korean.  Make It Yours  🪟 Liquid Glass Theme — Apple-inspired translucent glass aesthetic powered by Windows Acrylic blur. Your wallpaper shows through the bar.  🎨 Bar Textures — 6 built-in themes (Galaxy, Sakura, Noise, Ocean, Avatar World, Good Bad Souls) or load your own image. Supports JPEG, PNG, WebP, BMP.  🎨 Accent Color System — Choose from 8 preset colors applied instantly across the entire UI.  📐 UI Scale — Adjust bar size from 60% to 115%. Perfect fit for any screen size.  🖥️ Multi-Monitor Support — Per-monitor fullscreen detection. Playing a game on Monitor 1? The bar on Monitor 2 stays visible. Position corrects automatically when switching displays.  Why DockBar?  Your desktop is already cluttered. The taskbar isn't enough, widget panels take up space. DockBar is different: it's like a thin line sitting at the very top of your screen. It's there, but never in your way. When you need it, everything is visible at a glance.  65–75 MB memory usage (may increase with Liquid Glass, textures, or multiple widgets enabled). Low CPU impact. Auto-hides during fullscreen apps and games.  First Time Setup  After installing, open Settings to configure DockBar for your setup. Features like Auto-hide, Glass Effect, UI Scale, and display selection are off or at defaults — adjust them to match your screen size, monitor layout, and preferences. Taking a minute to explore Settings will give you the best experience.  Active Development  DockBar is constantly evolving. New widgets, new features, and improvements based on community feedback are released regularly. When you buy DockBar, you're not just getting today's product — you're getting every future update too.  From the Developer  A solo project I built from scratch. I made DockBar for myself — I wanted one place to reach everything I constantly need on my desktop. Then I thought, maybe others want that too. I read every piece of feedback and do my best to act on what makes sense. Thanks for the support.

A girl in a cat-eared hat and pink glasses settles into a corner of your desktop, keeping you company while you work, study, browse the web or enjoy a quiet moment.  Place her wherever you like and choose a wallpaper to make the desktop your own. Let her stay quietly by your side while you're busy, then take a break and watch her eyes follow your cursor, adding a little cuteness to an ordinary day at your computer.  She blinks, breathes and looks your way  The game includes one built-in little sister character. Natural blinking, breathing and gentle movements bring her to life on your desktop. Her head and eyes follow your cursor, while her long hair and clothing sway softly with her movements.  Find the right place for her    Click and hold the character to drag her. Hover over her and use the mouse wheel to resize her from 55% to 450%.    Toggle always-on-top mode to keep her in front of other windows or let them cover her.    Mouse input passes through transparent areas around and within the character. Enable Lock to let it pass through the entire character.    Hide her when you need to focus, then show her again from the system tray menu. Any active animated wallpaper keeps playing while she is hidden.    Use the right-click and system tray menus to open settings, switch characters and wallpapers, lock, hide or exit. You can also show or hide the taskbar icon.    Give your desktop a view you love  The game includes a pink-and-lavender static background and an animated version with drifting light and dust motes. Let your little sister share the desktop with this gentle scenery, or hide her and enjoy the wallpaper on its own.    Choose a local GIF animation or MP4 video as an animated wallpaper that loops silently behind your desktop icons.    Switch between built-in wallpapers and downloaded, compatible Workshop wallpapers in the Select Wallpaper menu.    Turn off the wallpaper feature to restore the desktop background recorded before you enabled it.    Animated wallpapers play while the game is running. MP4 playback depends on the video's encoding and your system's decoding support.  Discover more combinations in the Workshop  Steam Workshop has separate Characters and Wallpapers categories. Find community creations you like, or share compatible content you have made yourself.    Browse, search, subscribe to or unsubscribe from community characters and wallpapers. Once downloaded, choose them from the corresponding menu.    Upload compatible character packages, or share PNG/JPG static wallpapers, GIF/MP4 animated wallpapers and preview images.    Manage your published Workshop content: update its files and description, or delete your own creations.    Community content must use formats supported by the game. Character animation depends on the model resources used.  Your desktop preferences, remembered  Character position, size, language and display preferences are saved automatically for your next session. Placement can be restored across multiple monitors and is adjusted to the currently available screen area.  Steam Cloud can sync preferences such as character size, position and language. You must be signed in to Steam with cloud sync enabled. Local wallpaper files and Windows startup settings remain on the current computer.  Starting with Windows is supported and disabled by default on first use. You can turn it on in settings if you want to, and turn it off again at any time. Only one instance of the game runs at a time to prevent duplicate launches.  Feel at home in your language  The interface supports 30 languages. On first launch, the game prioritizes your Steam interface language when choosing its initial language. You can change it in settings at any time, and your choice will be remembered. name: One duck too many
lang: English, Traditional Chinese
short: A tiny bathtub sits on top of your taskbar with one duck in it. Its bubbles hatch more ducks, those ducks hatch more, and soon they spill over the rim and wander across your desktop. A desktop companion with 30 ducks to discover, born from the water's temperature, the night and each other.
about: You started with one duck. Now they own your desktop.  One Duck Too Many: Duck Habitat is a desktop companion. A small bathtub sits along the bottom of your screen, just above the taskbar or Dock, and stays on top while you work. It starts with a single yellow duck. Wherever nothing is drawn, your clicks go straight through to the windows underneath, so it never gets in the way.  A pond that runs itself  Ducks float, swim, nap, quack and blow bubbles. The bubbles drift up and collect themselves; they are what you spend. Every so often a big bubble rises with a duckling inside. You never have to click anything, but you can: pet a duck and it squeaks and hops, pick it up and toss it, pop a floating bubble for five times its worth.        From one duck to a king  The first half hour tells the whole story in the name. One duck becomes a few, then a crowd that stacks itself into towers. The tub fills, the ducks climb over the rim and start walking across your desktop, and at fifty ducks the pond crowns a king who leads parades along the bottom of your screen, then calls every duck together into one enormous Duck Mountain, with the king on top, until it all comes tumbling down. After that the pond settles into an easy idle pace, up to 250 ducks (or 500, if your computer is up for it).        30 ducks, and how they happen  A newborn usually takes after a duck nearby, but the bath and what the ducks get up to change it. It is never a plain lottery:   Cold water hatches Ice Ducks; the Hot Spring's boiling water hatches Lava Ducks. When ice meets lava, a Steam Duck puffs out.   On nights the Moon Lamp is lit, Moon Ducks glow in the water. When most of the pond falls asleep late at night, a Ghost Duck drifts up.   Too crowded for too long, five ducks fuse into a Giant. Two identical ducks asleep side by side for long enough wake up as one Two-Headed Duck.   A chain of ten bonks in a row leaves something golden behind. All eight colours in the pond at once bring a Rainbow Duck.   And when the whole pond is asleep in the dead of night, something wakes at the bottom of the tub.   8 colours, 6 hats (bow, sprout, party hat, shower cap, top hat, sunglasses), 2 sizes and 14 special ducks fill a 30-entry Duckdex. Ducks you haven't found yet show as silhouettes with a hint.  Ducks that live together   Real physics: ducks bump, squeak and knock each other out of the tub. A big splash startles the sleepers, and their landings startle the next ones: chain reactions.   One quack sets off the ducks around it, in waves across the pond.   Ducklings line up behind their mother. Parades march out of the tub, across your desktop and back.   Duck towers stack up and topple. Everyone fights over the beach ball. The slide sends ducks splashing into the crowd.   Too many ducks  Peaceful Pond, Crowded Pond, Duck Apocalypse. Once the tub is full, ducks spill over and wander, nap and pile up along the bottom of your screen; past twice what the tub holds, the desktop is theirs. A bigger tub pushes the tide back, for a while. If you'd rather keep them all in the tub, there's a setting for that.        Upgrades you can see  Everything you buy appears next to the tub and changes how the ducks live:   Bubble Machine (3 levels): more bubbles, more ducklings.   Bigger Tub (4 levels): more room before it gets crowded.   Beach Ball, Bubble Slide, Hot Spring, Moon Lamp, and the Duck Magnet, which pulls the whole pond together every so often.   Mystery Soap: seven soaps that change the next few ducklings, from strawberry pink to clear glass and gold leaf.   As much or as little as you like  Nothing dies, nothing is lost and nothing nags. While the game is closed the pond keeps blowing bubbles at half speed and raises a few ducklings (up to 8 hours' worth). Day and night follow your computer's clock. Ambient mode keeps it quiet and only announces new discoveries. A plaque on the tub shows your bubbles, your ducks and what the pond is working toward. A separate window holds

name: ResToggle
lang: English, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain, Simplified Chinese, Korean
short: Ultra-fast native utility for competitive gamers: instantly toggle between high-res native desktop displays and stretched resolutions for competitive FPS titles at maximum refresh rate, using 1-click desktop shortcuts or the system tray.
about: INSTANT RESOLUTION SWITCHER FOR ESPORTS & 1-CLICK DESKTOP SHORTCUTS  ResToggle Studio is a high-performance native utility designed for instant display resolution management and 1-click desktop shortcut generation. Built specifically for competitive gamers, streamers, and esports enthusiasts who frequently switch between native high-definition desktop displays (e.g., 1440p / 4K @ 165Hz / 240Hz / 360Hz) and customized stretched resolutions (4:3, 16:10, 5:4) for competitive first-person shooters and esports titles.  KEY FEATURES  • Instant Win32 Transitions (<1ms): Switch display configurations instantly using low-level native Win32 APIs, with zero extended black screens, zero terminal window flashes, and no system lag.  • Native 1-Click Desktop Shortcuts (.lnk): Generate native Windows shortcuts (.lnk) directly on your desktop. Double-click to instantly toggle between your Desktop Resolution and Gaming Resolution with zero overhead, leaving no stray executable files or triggering antivirus false positives.  • 1-Click System Tray Integration: Minimize to the taskbar tray for ultra-fast single-click resolution switching, or right-click to access quick presets and settings.  • Esports Competitive Preset Deck: Ready-to-use tournament presets for the most popular stretched aspect ratios:    - 4:3 Stretched: 1920x1440, 1440x1080, 1280x960, 1024x768    - 16:10 Stretched: 1728x1080, 1680x1050    - 5:4 Ultra-Stretch: 1280x1024    - 16:9 Standard: 1920x1080, 1280x720  • Maximum Refresh Rate & Multi-Monitor Preservation: Never lose high refresh rates; maintains 144Hz, 165Hz, 240Hz, 360Hz, or 500Hz without degradation and perfectly preserves spatial coordinates and secondary monitor alignment.  • Comprehensive GPU Hardware Support (AMD, NVIDIA, Intel): Dedicated hardware detection and built-in step-by-step guides for Full Panel GPU scaling on AMD Radeon (RX 7000/6000/5000 and APUs with FreeSync support), NVIDIA GeForce, and Intel graphics.  • 10-Second Safety Test Mode: Test any display mode with an interactive 10-second countdown timer and automatic baseline reversion if unconfirmed.  • Real-Time Engine Diagnostics: Built-in event monitor with timestamped logging, one-click clipboard export, and clear Win32 User32 error translation.  • Zero External Dependencies & Zero Bloatware: 100% pure C++17 compiled into a single lightweight x64 executable. No external runtimes required , Python, Java, or Electron), less than 5 MB of RAM usage, and instant startup.  • Windows 11 Fluent Dark UI: Modern dark theme with native rounded corners, immersive DWM titlebars, and customizable accent colors.  WHY CHOOSE RESTOGGLE STUDIO  In competitive first-person shooters, playing on a stretched aspect ratio (such as 4:3) widens target player models on screen, making tracking and precision aiming significantly easier while maximizing framerates and lowering input latency. However, returning to your native display resolution for everyday browsing, video editing, or productivity usually requires navigating slow, cumbersome graphics driver control panels.  ResToggle Studio removes all the friction: once your two profiles are configured (Desktop Mode and Game Mode), switch between them effortlessly in under a second via a clean desktop shortcut or directly from your system tray.  HOW IT WORKS IN 3 STEPS  1. Select your target display and define your native Desktop Resolution (e.g., 2560x1440 @ 240Hz).  2. Choose your preferred competitive stretched preset (e.g., 1280x960 @ 240Hz) or enter custom dimensions.  3. Click "Create Desktop Shortcut" or use the system tray icon: seamlessly toggle between resolutions anytime with a single click.  SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS  Minimum:  • OS: Windows 10 64-bit (Build 19041 or higher) or Windows 11 64-bit  • Processor: Any 64-bit Intel or AMD CPU  • Memory: 64 MB RAM  • Graphics: Any DirectX 11 / WDDM compatible GPU with resolution change support (NVIDIA, AMD Radeon, or Intel)  • Storage: 10 MB available spa

name: Superpower Rally: Home Guard
lang: French, German, Spanish - Spain, Ukrainian, Russian, Turkish, Japanese, Polish, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Korean, Portuguese - Brazil, Portuguese - Portugal, Spanish - Latin America, English
short: Relaxing light roguelike tower defense! Roguelike progression, plant hero growth, selectable super plants, day/night modes. Awakened plants vs zombies—collect plants, unlock skills, upgrade sun economy, defend your home. Low-spec friendly for tower defense and roguelike Build fans.
about: A relaxing, strategic, long-lasting light roguelike tower defense game! The game combines light Roguelike random progression, plant hero development, selectable super plants, and day/night dual modes. If you are looking for a tower defense game, then this title is absolutely for you.            🌍 Worldview: When Plants Awaken, Humanity's Last Hope Is Ignited  In the distant future, Earth's sky is shrouded in a thick gray haze, and sunlight grows weaker by the day. Among the ruins of cities, the once-prosperous human civilization has long retreated into underground shelters, while the surface world has been occupied by a mysterious and greedy force — the Zombie Legion.  However, just when humanity was on the brink of despair, an unexpected discovery changed everything — the plants have awakened. They have transformed into super plant heroes, vowing to protect this last homeland.  You will serve as the commander, leading these awakened plant heroes to resist wave after wave of zombie hordes and defend your home.  🌱 Rich Plant System: Every Plant Is Its Own Independent Tactic  The game features a rich plant system. Different plants have different skills, trajectories, attack methods, and corresponding super skills. Whether you prefer long-range sniping, area bombing, slow control, or high-burst instant kills, you can find your own core plant.     Trajectory Differences : Straight-line shots, parabolic throws, spread shots, bouncing, piercing, area explosions, and many other attack methods     Super Skills : Every plant has an exclusive ultimate skill that can turn the tide at critical moments     Plant Encyclopedia : Collect and cultivate different plants to build your own plant legion              🎯 Roguelike Random Progression: Every Run Is a Brand-New Experience  Each run allows you to manually choose one plant you like as your super plant to cultivate. Collecting a specified number of specific plants can unlock super plants and their corresponding exclusive powerful skills, helping you clear stages more effectively. In addition, you must be careful of various Boss skills!     Selectable Super Plants : Freely choose your core plant at the start of each run and build your own playstyle     Random Affixes and Enhancements : Randomly obtain enhancement options after each wave, with Build combinations     Unlock Exclusive Skills : Collect specified plants to unlock the ultimate exclusive skills of super plants    ☀️ Sun Orb Economy: Tempo Control Is the Key to Victory  The number of sun orbs in the game is very important. Unlocking more sun orbs at the right time can yield twice the result with half the effort.    Reasonably allocate sun orbs to balance in-battle economic development and combat power improvement    Seize the timing of unlocking to expand battlefield advantages              🌙 Day and Night: Dual-Mode Battlefield  The game is divided into day and night game modes. Battlefield environments, enemy behavior, and plant performance all differ under different modes.    Different modes bring completely different strategic ideas and stage-clearing experiences    If you cannot win, it does not matter. You can accumulate resources in each battle and use accumulated resources to upgrade plants, thereby clearing various difficulty stages    📈 Light Progression + Long-Term Playability: The More You Play, the Stronger You Get, and the Stronger You Get, the More Satisfying It Feels  This is a light roguelike tower defense game that can be played for a very long time. Even if you fail a run, you can still gain permanent progression resources and gradually become stronger.     Meta Progression : Upgrade plants, unlock new plants, and improve basic attributes     Stage Progression : From normal mode to challenge mode, difficulty increases layer by layer     Suitable for Long-Term Play : Relaxing and casual, no grinding, no pay-to-win, play a round anytime, anywhere    💻 Low Configuration Requirements: Meets the Needs of Most PC Play

name: Acuaria Pet Desktop
lang: Spanish - Spain, English
short: A beautiful contemplative game that turns your desktop into a pond where you can care for your own fish with a variety of colors and shapes. Design their colors, patterns, and shapes as you watch them grow, reproduce, and pass on their traits to the next generation.
about: Welcome to Acuaria!   Imagine turning your desktop into a vibrant and relaxing pond where you can design and care for your own fish while working or performing other tasks on your PC. In this beautiful aquatic simulation game, you have full control to customize each of your fish, from head to tail, choosing from a wide variety of colors, patterns, and shapes, as well as a challenging achievement system linked to their breeding. Creativity knows no bounds!   Key Features:      Unique Fish Design:  Choose from a vast palette of colors and patterns to create unique and stunning fish. Do you prefer a fish with bright stripes or something more subtle like soft scales? The choice is yours!     Dynamic Life Cycle:  Watch as your fish grow, breed, and pass on their traits to the next generation. Each fish is a small work of art that evolves before your eyes. Fish reach adulthood after 20 minutes and grow old and die at 45 minutes, so make sure to breed them before it’s too late!     Achievements and Challenges:  Unlock achievements as you explore new combinations of colors, patterns, and shapes with the breeding system. Become the master of fish and achieve all hidden milestones, including creating the elusive legendary fish!     Relaxing Simulation:  Enjoy watching your creations swim peacefully and follow each other around your desktop. With a relaxed, unhurried gameplay style, it’s perfect for unwinding and interacting with your aquatic ecosystem.     Star-Rated Fish Buying and Selling System:   Your fish don’t just grow and breed – they can also be sold to earn in-game money! Each fish has a value that varies based on its growth stage and the stars it earns. When a fish reaches its maximum growth potential, it receives stars based on its unique characteristics and generation count. The more stars a fish has, the more valuable it is, and you can breed it to pass down even more value to its offspring!     Buying New Fish:  Use the money you earn from selling your fish to acquire new ones or improve your aquarium. The combination of rare, well-designed fish with many generations behind them can bring great profits.     Star System:  When a fish reaches adulthood, it receives between 1 to 5 stars, depending on its price and special traits. A 5-star fish is a true gem in the aquarium, and its sale can generate significant revenue to reinvest in new creations.     Strategic Reinvestment:  Sell and breed your higher-star fish to generate income and use those resources to buy unique fish or expand your personalized fish collection. This cycle allows you to continually improve your aquarium and reach greater achievements.     What Makes It Special?   This is not just a game; it’s a unique creative relaxation experience in the form of desktop pets.  Whether you’re looking for a game to unwind with while you work or want to test your skills as a creator and seller of rare fish, this digital aquarium will keep you hooked!

about: Build a new home with your forest companions  *Beastwood Haven* is a relaxing creature-collecting and camp-building game that blends production management, exploration, and automated turn-based combat.  Choose your first companion and begin life in a modest woodland camp. Plan roads and buildings, assign creatures to jobs that suit their specialties, and turn gathering, crafting, cooking, and rest into a connected camp routine.  Venture into different environments, build teams around your companions' elements, condition, and equipment, and face other forest creatures in automated turn-based battles. Return with useful materials and mysterious eggs, then hatch and raise companions with their own personalities and talents.  Turn expedition materials into meals, equipment, and skill upgrades, then expand your camp and take on more dangerous regions. Work and travel cause fatigue, while weather and special events alter production and exploration conditions. Rotate teams, schedule rest, and prepare supplies to keep the haven running.  Once your camp is flourishing, construct its ultimate facility and venture into the final region deep within the forest. Or slow down, complete the codex, care for your companions, and let a chosen creature accompany you as a desktop pet.
