name: Donatello
lang: English
short: Turn one 2D character image into animated sprite sheets and a skeletal 2D character for Spine or DragonBones. Use your own art, or create the image in the app. Motion comes from a built-in library or your own clips. Runs entirely on your machine.
about: From a Drawing — or a 3D Model — to an Animated 2D Character   Donatello  is a local desktop studio that turns characters into animation-ready 2D skeletal assets for Spine and DragonBones — completely on your machine, with no cloud uploads and no subscriptions. You can start from  a single 2D image . Feed it a concept sketch or a piece of key art and Donatello builds a 3D character from it on your own hardware, then converts that into a cut-up, bone-driven 2D rig. Already have a rigged 3D model? Bring it and skip straight to the conversion. Either way you finish with sprites, a bone hierarchy and animations that drop into Unity, Unreal Engine, Godot, or any engine with a Spine or DragonBones runtime.   How It Works     Start  from a single reference image, or load a rigged 3D character (FBX, GLB, GLTF).      Choose your angle  — a 3/4 view or a side view, facing either direction.      Generate  — Donatello cuts the character into sprites and binds them to a 2D skeleton for you.      Animate  — pick clips from the built-in library, or bring motion from your own FBX, BVH, GLB or Spine files.      Export  — Spine JSON with a packed texture atlas, or a DragonBones JSON package.     Key Features     Image to Character:  Build a 3D character from one image with on-device AI (TRELLIS.2 or TripoSplat), then convert it to a 2D rig. Nothing is uploaded at generation time. Needs a reasonably capable GPU — the app checks your machine and tells you what it can run.      3D to 2D Conversion:  Automatic sprite cutting and skinning from any rigged 3D source.      Camera Angles:  3/4 and side views, in either facing direction.       Built-in Animation Library:  Hundreds of ready-to-use clips — walk, run, idle, attack, jump, reactions — adapted to your character. No source animation required.      Bring Your Own Motion:  Retarget from your FBX, GLB or BVH files, or append animations from an existing Spine project onto a character you did not make in Donatello.      Animation Fine-Tuning:  Per-clip controls for speed, amplitude, bounce, squash & stretch, follow-through and joint bias. Shape the feel of every motion without touching a keyframe.      Auto-Rigging:  Humanoid auto-rigging on CPU, Apple Silicon and NVIDIA GPUs. Adaptive rigging for non-humanoid characters on supported NVIDIA hardware.      Beyond Humanoids:  Bipeds are fully supported. Quadrupeds, arachnids, winged creatures, dragons, fish, dinosaurs and limbless characters ship as experimental profiles.      Spine & DragonBones Export:  Spine JSON (4.0 format) with texture atlas, or DragonBones 5.5-compatible JSON.      100% Local & Private:  Everything runs on your workstation. Your models, reference images and generated assets never leave your machine.   Built for Game Developers & Technical Artists    Whether you are an indie dev turning concept art into a playable character, a technical artist who needs a few hundred retargeted clips by tomorrow, or a pipeline engineer automating the 3D-to-2D step — Donatello does the tedious part so you can focus on the game.     Spine and DragonBones output compatible with Unity, Unreal Engine, Godot, and custom engines.     Works out of the box with standard humanoid rigs, including Mixamo.     Complex source skeletons are simplified automatically to a bone count that performs well in 2D.     Preview your character and scrub its animations before exporting.      AI workflow  Donatello uses AI to automate tedious work. Image-to-3D reconstruction and automatic segmentation are fast starting points; results vary by character complexity and will often benefit from manual review and small touch-ups.  System Notes   The core 3D-to-2D workflow runs on any supported machine. AI features (Image-to-3D, auto-rigging) require additional hardware — see System Requirements below. AI models are downloaded on first use and cached locally; they add between  2 GB and 15 GB  to your disk usage depending on which models you activate.

name: Scrapping Simulator

about: ⚙️ Scrapping Simulator   A low-poly first-person simulator set in a stylised Australian take on the global e-waste crisis.      Step into the steel-capped boots of an Aussie E-Waste Scrapper.     Hunt down discarded electronics, dismantle them piece-by-piece, and extract valuable materials like  Copper ,  Silver , and  Gold , along with lower-value materials such as Iron, Aluminium, Brass, and Plastic.  Sell your scrap for cash, manage your expenses and fluctuating market prices, and expand your operation through smart investments and upgrades.  Every playthrough is shaped by your choices and deep dynamic systems: daily e-waste variety, weather-affected solar power, hundreds of component combinations inside E-Waste, and ever-changing market prices.  A New Game includes a short guided tutorial (10-15 minutes) on Day 1 where time is frozen and energy is capped. Use this time to explore and learn the systems at your own pace. In-game manuals are also available for deeper dives into mechanics.  Best suited for players who enjoy hands-on tasks, meaningful progression, and managing real-world inspired challenges.   Important Clarification:   This is a realism-inspired simulator, not a sandbox destruction game. While dismantling electronics is a core detailed part of the experience, the game also includes bills, financial management, consequences to actions, and many interconnected systems. These elements seem to catch some players off-guard. If you're looking for a carefree sandbox game with no responsibilities, consequences or progression, this may not be the game for you. An Endless Sandbox Mode is not currently planned.       🛠️ Features      🔍 Scavenge & Salvage   Head out early each morning to secure the best finds before rival scrappers beat you to them. Not all junk is worth your time, learning what to take (and what to leave behind) is part of the strategy. Pull Items apart down to the last Screw and gather the Raw Materials hidden inside.   📈 Watch the Market   Track fluctuating prices on your in-game PC. Sell raw or refined metals at the  Scrap Yard , offload low-tier electronics at the  Pawn Shop  to free up time and storage for higher-value targets. Timing and focus can directly impact your profits.   🛒 Upgrade Your Tools    Visit the Hardware Store to purchase better tools to speed up disassembly, solar panels to reduce utility costs & provide idle income, improved item transport options, expanded external storage, and other efficiency-focused upgrades. Spend wisely, not every upgrade provides immediate returns, managing your responsibilities alongside Upgrade purchases is essential.   🔥  Smelt & Refine   In the mid-to-late game, reinvest your profits into a  Furnace Set ,  Crucible , and  Ingot Moulds  to turn low-value raw Base Metals into high-value ingots. Further into the late game, unlock the  Chemical Set  to refine pure Gold and Silver for premium returns.  The Furnace & Chemical Sets as glamorous as they sound,  do not  start producing Ingots out of thin air. These systems take Valuable Raw Metals you've hopefully been  accumulating for this very moment, to smelt & refine them into more valuable Ingots.   💪 Level Up & Unlock Perks   Earn XP in  Disassembling ,  Trading , and  Scavenging  to level-up and gain perk points across three distinct skill trees. Specialise your playstyle and refine your strategy to maximise productivity and long-term profit.    Disassembly too slow?  Lean into the Disassembly Skill Tree to improve both Materials Gained and Base Disassembly Speed.   Not enough Items around to keep moving forward?  Lean into the Scavenging Skill Tree which will produce more Items for you to Scrap and allow you to carry more Raw Materials.   Can't earn enough Money to sustain your lavish playstyle?  Lean into the Trading Skill Tree which Improves Buying & Selling Prices to various Stores.  🧩  E-Waste You’ll Deconstruct:      LCDs & CRT TVs      Desktop Computers &a

Quickly find your cursor, or follow your cursor with a large mouse indicator visual. This product is available natively in English, but it has automated translations for most major languages. Settings:  Mouse Display (Default: False) If enabled, a visual representation of your mouse will follow the cursor, making it clear to viewers what the mouse is doing and what buttons are being pressed.   Mouse Display Background (Default: #40ADD8E6) Changes the background color of the display mouse.   Mouse Display Background Pressed (Default: #8080FFFF) Changes the background color of the display mouse when pressed.   Mouse Display Border (Default: #40FFFFFF) Changes the border color of the display mouse.   Mouse Display Layout (Default: 15,0,50,100) Controls the offset and size of the mouse display.   Mouse Display Follow (Default: True) Mouse display will follow the cursor with the offset specified in the Mouse Display Layout configuration.   Cursor Finder (🖰?) Helps you keep track of your cursor.  When enabled, shaking your mouse will temporarily put a spotlight on your cursor.  Settings:  Cursor Finder (Default: False) If you lose track of your cursor, this feature can put a visual indicator around the cursor temporarily to help you out.  All you need to do is wave the mouse around like a crazy person.   Cursor Finder Opacity (Default: 0.62) Controls how visible the cursor highlighting will be when shaken.   Cursor Finder Shake Distance (Default: 4) Controls how intense the mouse shake needs to be to trigger the cursor finder.   Cursor Finder Shake Amount (Default: 6) Controls how much mouse shaking is needed to be to trigger the cursor finder.   Cursor Finder Always On Opacity (Default: 0) Controls how visible the cursor highlighting will be at all times.   Cursor Finder Invisible Cursor (Default: False) Unless you turn this feature on, the cursor highlighting feature will be automatically disabled when the cursor is not visible.   Deep Cursor Visibility Check (Default: False) When checking whether or not a cursor is visible, sometimes a deeper check is required.  The deep cursor check has some performance implications, though likely not noticeable.  Keep this off if you aren't noticing any problems with how the tool reacts to invisible cursors.   Mouse Wheel Accelerator (🖰⇳💨) This is a simple customizable mouse wheel accelerator.   By default, mouse wheel speed doubles at level 1, triples at level 2, and quadruples at level 3, but you can configure these multipliers.   Using any input modification features puts you at risk with multiplayer gaming.  Each game has its own rules on where it draws the line between cheating and not cheating.  Some don't care, some will kick you, and some might ban you.  This product does its part in cooperating with anti-cheat software by not hiding the source of input, so any game could easily ignore injected input if programmed to do so.   This feature is generally not particularly useful for cheating in multiplayer games, but still faces some risk of being considered cheating.  In order to work correctly, the feature may produce 2 mouse wheel events for 1 hardware event, which technically does not comply with the common rule of 1 user input to 1 game input. name: Keyboard Kingdom
lang: English
short: Your keyboard is a kingdom. Place it on your desktop and keep working: every keystroke grows your castle and fights off waves of monsters. In a spare moment, level up your keys, choose laws and hire heroes to boost your kingdom. Then start over, stronger than before.
about: Your keyboard is a kingdom  Type, code, write, chat. Keyboard Kingdom grows while you work.  Place the game on your desktop and forget about it. Every key you press sends its strength to your castle and to the monsters at the gates. No clicking, no switching windows, no waiting for a timer.          Every keystroke counts  Each key is its own character in your kingdom. The more you press a key, the stronger it becomes. Your favorite keys will grow first, and a key's progress is never lost, even when you start a new run.  Grow your castle, fight the waves  Two things grow from the same keystroke:     The castle  collects experience. Each new level lets you choose a law.     The monster waves  take damage. Defeat a whole wave to reach the next one, and collect coins from every hit.    Each one makes your keys stronger against the other. Push both forward, or choose one and go deep.          Choose laws  Every castle level offers three random laws. Pick one. Take the same law again and it gets stronger. Some laws help every key, others help only certain keys or certain heroes. Build your own set of rules for each run.          Hire heroes  Spend your coins on heroes and place them on your keys. Every hero has a race, a class and their own special effect: one strengthens nearby keys, another presses neighbor keys for you. But a hero's life is limited. Every use of the key costs life, so plan where you place them.  Some races and classes are strong against certain monsters and weak against others. Learn the monsters of each wave and choose your team to match.          Start over, stronger  When progress becomes slow, begin a new run. Heroes, coins and laws are reset, but your keys keep their levels and your best castle and wave levels keep giving permanent bonuses. Try another castle or wave. Each one has its own rule and its own reward.          Play and work at the same time  Most of the game happens by itself while you type. When you have a spare minute, open the game, spend your coins, choose a law, level up a key, and go back to work.  And also    Keys: as many as your keyboard has (we counted)    Races: [N]     Classes: [N]    Castles: [N]    Dungeons: 18    Monsters: 100    Passive play while you work, active play in a spare moment

name: ColorFarm
lang: English, French, Spanish - Spain, Simplified Chinese
short: A cozy farming companion that lives in the corner of your desktop. Earn coins through everyday keyboard and mouse activity, grow colorful plants, turn each harvest into bead-art materials, create freely from patterns, collect your artwork, and expand your own floating farms.
about: One-line Pitch   Grow colors in a little desktop farm, then turn every harvest into bead art of your own.     Short Description   A cozy farming companion that lives in the corner of your Windows desktop. Earn coins through everyday keyboard and mouse activity, grow colorful plants, turn each harvest into bead-art materials, create freely from patterns, collect your artwork, and expand your own floating farms.     About This Game    A Little Farm to Share Your Day   ColorFarm is a cozy farming companion that lives on your Windows desktop. Tuck it into a corner while you work, study, or browse, and let your plants keep growing. Whenever you need a short break, open the farm, water a few crops, and see which colors are ready to harvest.     Let Everyday Activity Feed Your Farm   Keyboard presses, mouse clicks, scrolling, and mouse movement can become coins. There are no daily checklists demanding your attention. Your ordinary computer activity naturally helps the farm move forward.  The game only counts input totals and overall mouse travel distance. It never records which keys you press, what you type, or your mouse coordinates.     Grow Plants and Collect Colors.    Unlock plants with coins or diamonds, then sow, water, and harvest them across multiple floating farms. Every plant has its own color, growing time, and yield. Care for each plot yourself, or let a floating farm bot handle the routine at your preferred pace.     The Shape Is Fixed. The Color Is Yours.   Harvested plants become materials for bead art. A pattern defines only the shape of a piece—it never forces you to use a specific color. Follow the suggested palette, or remake the same pattern with a completely different set of plants.  You can also import your own images as patterns. Place beads one at a time, paint continuously, use the fill bucket and missing-cell finder, then collect, inspect, rename, and export your finished artwork as a PNG.     Build a Tiny World of Your Own   Completing bead art earns diamonds that can unlock upgrades, new farms, farm bots, and cosmetic items. Rename farms and artwork, choose a favorite frame, and gradually turn a quiet corner of your desktop into a colorful world of your own.     Gentle, Quiet, and Never in a Hurry   ColorFarm is a premium single-player game. Plants continue to grow, offline progress is supported, and there are no mandatory daily chores. Stay focused when you need to, and return to your farm whenever you feel like taking a small break.     Feature Summary   - A transparent, movable, and compactable Windows desktop farm  - Earn coins through ordinary keyboard and mouse activity without recording input content  - Plant, water, harvest, and manage multiple floating farms  - Turn harvested plants into materials for freely colored bead art  - Import custom patterns, collect finished artwork, and export it as PNG files  - Let farm bots plant, water, and harvest automatically  - Play offline at your own pace, with offline growth and no mandatory daily chores

name: SoulForge Legends
lang: English**
short: Twelve classes, one open world, and up to five of you in it. A co-op action RPG: hunt world bosses, build your character your way, then fight where skill beats gear every time, from a 40-player free-for-all to ranked 1v1, 2v2 and 3v3. Or go Forsworn: solo permadeath survival. One life, one holdfast.
about: Twelve classes. One open world. Endless legends.     SoulForge Legends is a co-op action RPG set on Aerethia, a world torn between two factions: the Elarian and the Legion. Pick a class, build it however you like, and go make a name for yourself. Play solo, or bring up to four friends along for the ride. The whole game is player-hosted, which is the part I'm proudest of. There's no subscription and no server cost.   When you group up, one player hosts the world directly over Steam and everyone jumps in. And you never have to worry about your progress: everything you earn is tied to your account and safely backed up, so your characters won't disappear.    Play on your desktop tonight, log in from your laptop tomorrow, and it's all right where you left it.   Twelve classes, and they actually play differently     The Vanguard holds the line behind a shield. The Chronoweaver messes with time. The Hellborn throws infernal magic around, the Stormcaller chains lightning between enemies, and there are eight more besides. Every class has its own    skills, its own talent tree to grow into, and its own look. Find the one that clicks and get good with it.        A world worth getting lost in     Aerethia is one connected map you roam at your own pace. Go quiet and solo, or fill it with your party and cause some    trouble. There are roaming Champions to hunt, world bosses that turn up daily, hourly events to drop into, materials to gather, and professions to level. Levels don't lock your friends out either, so a high-level buddy can still play    alongside someone who just started.        Co-op without the headaches     Everyone gets a short 8-character friend ID. Add your friends, make a party of up to five, and you're all in the same world with one click. The leader hosts, but everyone keeps their own character and their own progress. Nobody fights    over loot, and nobody's stuck waiting for one specific person to log on before they can play.   You're never really alone out there     Even though you host your own games, there's a whole community running alongside you. A global chat ties everyone on Aerethia together, so you can talk, ask for a hand, show off, or just trade insults with a stranger. Meet someone you    get along with? Grab their friend ID, add them, and party up for real. You get a channel for your group, private whispers for one-on-one, and if you're feeling cocky, you can challenge another player straight to the Coliseum by    their ID. The friends you make here are yours to keep.        The Coliseum: no gear, just skill     Sometimes you just want to fight. The Coliseum throws you into a 40-player free-for-all where everyone is set to the    same power level. No stat advantage, no pay-to-win gear, nobody to blame but your own reflexes. Win fights, earn    badges, and spend them on cosmetics: trails, wings, titles, and some very petty flags you can plant on the people you    knock down.         Forty combatants, every single time: real players when they're around, Champions filling the rest. They hunt, they    fight each other, they plant flags on your corpse and talk trash in chat, and you won't always be sure which is which.    It also means the Coliseum works offline, whenever you want it.        Ranked, for when you want it to count     The Crucible is the serious side of PvP: ranked 1v1, 2v2 and 3v3, queued from anywhere in the world, with a rating    that actually moves. Same fixed power level, same cosmetic-only rewards. No    bots and no filler here, real opponents only. Climb as far as your skill takes you.        Survival Mode: one life, one holdfast     There's another way to play Aerethia, and it's a harder one. As a Forsworn you swear off both factions and walk into    the wilds alone: no party, no queues, nobody coming to help. Die once and that character is gone for good, along with    everything they built.    You claim your ground and raise a holdfast on it. A hearth, walls and gates, farms and a we

name: The Gigglebone Gang: AlphaBonk Farm
lang: English**
short: A is for AlphaBonk! Join Farmer Bonk and the Gigglebone Gang for a trip through the alphabet down on the farm — letters, rhymes, real farm photos and a barnyard full of silly games. A fully restored 1995 Headbone Interactive classic.
about: Down on AlphaBonk Farm, the alphabet has gotten loose. There's a letter for every animal and an animal for every letter, a rhyme waiting at each one, and Farmer Bonk has a story about pretty much everything. Velma the Swine has the facts. Bunji the Frog and Clyde the Parrot have the games. Nobody is in a hurry.     Originally released by Headbone Interactive in 1995 and now fully restored for modern desktops,  AlphaBonk Farm  is an A-to-Z ramble through farm life for brand-new readers — twenty-six letters, plenty of activities, and lots to explore with the Gigglebone Gang.    Key Features     The Whole Alphabet, A to Z:  Pick any letter off the strip and go. Have fun rhyming and reading the words together with the game.      Games For Every Letter:  Each letter hides either a Seek 'n' Find with Clyde — spot the objects tucked into the scene, with hints when you want them and a clock when you're feeling brave — or a Poke 'n' Prod with Bunji.      Barnyard Toy Boxes:  Have fun with Bunji in an Egg Factory, a Fishing Pond, a Haunted Barnyard, an Ice Cream Parlor, an X-Ray Lab, a Livestock Roundup, the Numbskull Nut Revue and an Upside-Down Room, among others.      Real Farm Photographs:  Switch to the Photo track and every letter opens onto real pictures of a working farm.      Fun Farm Facts with Velma:  Thirty-nine illustrated explainers about how a farm actually works, plus Farmer Bonk's own rambling anecdotes about the pictures.     Fully Restored 1995 Animation:  Hand-drawn cartoon art and a complete voice cast, rebuilt to run natively on modern machines. Everything is spoken aloud, so it works for ages 4 and up whether or not they can read yet.

name: Teen Hustler Demo
lang: English*, Russian*, Simplified Chinese**
short: Build your digital empire from a cramped room to a high-tech penthouse. Code, hack, mine crypto, and manipulate the dark web in this deep 3D economic sandbox simulator. Stay in the shadows, manage your hardware, and don't get caught by the police!
about: Your crypto wallet is empty, but your digital ambitions are limitless.    You play as a 20-year-old guy trying to survive and make money in the depths of the dark web  You start out in a cramped room with an old PC and a basic freelance app. From there, it's all up to you. Achieve success and conquer the shadow internet by any means necessary.  Take on legal coding contracts, build massive crypto farms, or forge your own unique path through ShadowNet via risky contracts—the possibilities in this massive hacking sandbox are endless. You've never played a simulator quite like this!  Work your way up from a cheap desk and slow internet to top-tier hardware, multi-monitor setups, and actual server rooms. Invest your money in volatile crypto markets and shadowy ventures. Succeed, make mistakes, and upgrade your gear. But don't forget to manage your energy, keep your PC cool, and stay in the shadows on your climb to the top.  Do you have the courage to build your own digital empire?  KEY FEATURES     Interactive 3D Room:  Manage your daily life and upgrade your living conditions. Earn enough to move from a run-down apartment in a dangerous neighborhood to a high-tech penthouse. Don't neglect your health: sleep, order food, and drink energy drinks to stay in the game 24/7.               Retro OS Simulation:  Work within a meticulously recreated operating system. Customize your desktop, chat with   clients, and complete legal orders via the GigLink messenger.              ShadowNet & Darknet:  Dive deep into the shadow internet. Take on illegal hacking contracts, manipulate databases, launder "dirty" money through crypto-mixers, and boost your illicit ratings. But be careful: every illegal action raises your police heat level. If the cops come for you, it’s Game Over.              Hardware & Mining Farms:  Build your ultimate dream PC. Purchase powerful processors, GPUs, and cooling systems. Configure them via the HEVIOS utility to speed up hacks and maximize your crypto mining yields             Exchange & Investments:  Buy low and sell high on the CoinTrade exchange. Invest your hard-earned capital into risky venture projects.              Hacking & Casino:  Play intense mini-hacks to bypass server security systems, and test your luck in the retro casino right from your desk when you have some downtime.

name: ALL HANDS LOST
lang: English**
short: A top-down mercenary space shooter. Take contracts across the Cassian Expanse, command a wing of fighters and drones, and hunt the pirate warlord Captain Bastard. Death costs your gear, cargo and half your credits; your data cores, ships and star charts carry on.
about: Outnumbered. Outgunned. Paid anyway. You're a mercenary captain in the Cassian Expanse, working the contracts nobody else will take. Your handler Nikki finds the work. Company officer Karl signs the cheques. And somewhere out past the blockades, the pirate warlord Captain Bastard has started to take an interest in you.  Break blockades, rescue stranded miners, escort cargo through raider space and raid pirate depots, all on the way to a showdown with the warlord himself. Command a wing Launch fighters and mining drones, give them targets and keep them alive. When you're outnumbered, your wing is your edge. Build your loadout Flak, phalanx, plasma, MIRVs, blades. Mix your weapons, manage their heat, and find what works for your ship. Salvage the gear you don't need for parts, and use them to rework the gear you keep. Contracts, not grind Pick your next job from the star map: blockades, rescues, escorts, assaults. Every contract has bonus objectives worth chasing, and the story pays better than farming ever will. Death has a price Die out there and you lose your gear, your cargo and half your credits. The company keeps what matters: your data cores, ship unlocks and star charts survive, and so does your progress through the story. Every run pushes you further in. The Expanse is bigger than one warlord    The Pirates.  Captain Bastard's raiders own the lanes. Take them back.    The Corpos.  Corporate interests watch from the edges of every contract, and they're keeping score.    The Crystals.  Crystal signatures keep turning up where they shouldn't. Your handler doesn't think it's a coincidence.    From the Rift.  Something ancient and wrong is transmitting from deep inside the Rift.   Features   Episode 1, "All Hands Lost": a 12-mission story campaign against Captain Bastard   Fast top-down ship combat with fighter wings, mining drones and heat-managed weapons   A star map of systems, lanes and jump gates to chart as you go   Forward bases you take from the pirates and retrofit as your own   Every ship, asteroid and explosion drawn in procedural vector art, rendered in light. No sprites anywhere.   Full gamepad support, with a dedicated Steam Deck build tested alongside every desktop release  ```

name: ChickenScratch: Cluck & Code
lang: English
short: You don't steer the chicken. You program it. Write real scripts in a fake desktop OS and send your bird into fields that reseed every run, so hardcoded coordinates work exactly once. Upgrades aren't +1% damage: they're if statements, for loops, and the memory to hold a list.
about: You don't steer the chicken.    There is no movement key. There is a terminal, a text editor, and a bird standing in a field waiting to be told what to do. You write a script, you press run, and you watch it work, or watch it walk into a hedge forty times while you read your own logic back and realise what you actually said.    var loot = Scanner.get_visible_drops()  if loot.size() > 0:      Chicken.move_east()      Chicken.pick_up()    That is the whole game. Everything else is pressure on it.           The language is real, and it is one you already know    ChickenScratch is syntactically identical to GDScript: significant indentation,  var  and  func ,  if  /  elif  /  else ,  for  and  while , Arrays and Dictionaries, integers that stay integers. Not a visual scripting toy, not a fake language with three verbs. It compiles to bytecode and runs on its own virtual machine, one instruction at a time, so you can watch the line your chicken is on.    If you have written code before, you will be productive in about ninety seconds. If you haven't, the game is built to teach you in the order the world makes you need things.           Upgrades are syntax    There is no damage percentage to buy. The shop sells  language .       Conditional Evaluation Node , 50 Corn. Now you have  if .     Iterative Processing Core , 50 Worms. Now you have  while  and  for .     Linear Memory Arrays , 100 Berries. Now you can hold a list of what you found.     Associative Memory Lattice , 350 Corn. Now you can remember where you have been.     Cartographic Compass , 500 Corn. Now you know where you are.      With nothing bought, your best script is a straight line of  move_west()  calls. That works, because a blocked step only costs you the step, and with no  if  in your script there is nothing listening for the failure anyway. Nine trips of that buys you the ability to ask a question. The curve is the ladder from "walk in a fixed direction and hope" to a real breadth-first search, and every rung is paid for by the last one.    The first two purchases are priced in different currencies on purpose, so you cannot farm one field and skip the other's lesson.           The world reseeds, so you cannot cheat    Every time your chicken walks back into the coop, all twenty-five zones regenerate. Layouts, drops, resources, where the crab is standing. All of it.    What a zone  is  never changes. The Corn Rows are always corn rows. But the route through them is new, which means a script that writes down coordinates works exactly once. The game ships one seed script,  hardcoded_trap.scratch , that exists purely to prove this to you.    Searching is the skill. The upgrades are what let you search better.           It is a whole fake operating system    The Coop is a desktop, and the terminal is the interface, not a menu with a terminal in it. Everything is a command.       ls ,  cd ,  cat ,  cp ,  mv ,  grep ,  more  and  less , with pipes and  &&  and  ;  chaining     vim  inside the terminal, with modes, operators, motions, visual mode,  /  search and  :%s/a/b/g  with a live preview. There is a plain editor window too, if you would rather     man  is the in-game compendium: the language, the API, the mechanics, and a bestiary that fills in as your chicken meets things     shop ,  stats , resizable translucent windows, a settings panel, and an inbox      Nobody explains the game to you in a tooltip. Your gran explains it, by email, because she left you the farm.           Errors are the game    When your script does something impossible, it does not fail silently and it does not throw an engine error at you. It tells you what you asked for and what was actually there:    [quote]line 8: There's no `x` in that. It has: type, position, health.[/quote]    A blocked move returns  false  rather than stopping. That is information, and it is how a good script finds a gap in a hedge without ever being told where the gap is. A move you cannot make n

short: Explore Gensokyo from an outsider's perspective in this old-school Touhou DRPG!
about: Sumireko Usami is not a normal high-schooler at all. She is so abnormal that even the fantasy land of Gensokyo considers her an anomaly. Truth is, she can visit Gensokyo in her dreams!      A new incident has occurred, and Gensokyo has a  clone problem         Artificial Dream in Arcadia is a first person dungeon crawler where the player, as Sumireko, has to navigate tricky mazes and capture a party of the strongest Touhou characters to assist them in turn-based battles. Go all over Gensokyo and beyond, to solve an incident which seems a little too convenient for Sumireko, seeing as she's the only person in Gensokyo who has a tool to control this infestation of clones: her newly-bought smartphone. A large selection of your favorite Touhou characters Clones are roaming the lands! They are known as Sleepers and take the shape of established Touhou characters, and as such, almost every Touhou character is represented and playable. Sumireko's phone is equipped with a special app that allows her to capture Sleepers by beating them in a round of Danmaku.            If you win, you can add them to your party, or turn them into useful items! You can also fuse multiple Sleepers together to make something new entirely. Adding Sleepers to your party will increase battery usage. If your phone runs out of battery charge, you will lose access to Sleepers and your Map, so always come prepared! name: Dungeons and Treasure 2
lang: English, German, Spanish - Spain, Russian, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean
short: Dungeons and Treasure II is a voxel action roguelike for 1-4 players. Brave endless, scaling floors with 100+ items, buffs, and permanent unlocks. Explore procedural zones with unique bosses, secrets, and traps. Features full controller support and mid-run saves for desktop play.
about: Dungeons and Treasure II: Game Overview   Dungeons and Treasure II  is a voxel-style action roguelike designed for desktop play with full support for controllers. It is an endless, fast-paced adventure where players navigate procedurally generated environments filled with unique enemies, traps, and boss encounters.  Core Gameplay and Structure  The game focuses on a continuous loop of exploration and combat. Players progress through handcrafted rooms that are stitched together randomly to ensure every run is different.     Endless Scaling:  The game does not have a final floor. Instead, the difficulty increases the longer you survive. As you progress through different loops, enemies gain new abilities, health, and damage, while the environment becomes more hazardous.     Persistent Progression:  While standard gold is lost upon death, defeating bosses rewards a special currency. This currency is used to permanently unlock new items, weapons, and companions, expanding the pool of gear available for future runs.     Save and Exit:  Progress can be saved at any time in single-player mode, allowing players to pause a run and return to it later.    Combat and Customization  Survival depends on the equipment and buffs collected throughout the dungeon. With over 100 different items, the game allows for a wide variety of combat styles.     Weapons and Shields:  Players can utilize melee and ranged weapons, each with distinct stats. Shields provide defensive options, requiring players to balance protection with aggressive play.     Buffs and Companions:  Passive upgrades can be stacked without a limit, allowing for significant power increases during a run. Additionally, companions can be found to assist in battle by attacking enemies or casting curses and buffs.     Active Items:  These provide specific effects that must be manually triggered, adding a layer of tactical timing to combat.    Environments and Hazards  Each environment features its own atmosphere and mechanical challenges.     Unique Bestiary:  Every zone contains 6 to 8 unique enemy types with specific behaviors. As the game loops, these enemies become more complex, eventually gaining multiple abilities.     Traps and Secrets:  Dungeons are filled with traps that can strike from any angle. Players will also encounter hidden rooms that contain either high-tier rewards or dangerous ambushes.     Navigation Tools:  Waypoints allow for fast travel between discovered areas and reveal larger portions of the map. A minimap is also available to track dropped items and explored tiles.    Multiplayer Features  The game is built to be played solo or with a group of up to 4 players through a flexible multiplayer system.       In-Game Economy:  Players can find shopkeepers within the dungeon to spend gold on items, including gear that has not yet been permanently unlocked.

name: AI Society
lang: English
short: Build a town or run a game studio, both staffed by AI characters with real personalities. Watch townsfolk work, argue, fight, and raid dungeons. Or play the RPG your own AI dev team designs, builds, and ships while you run the company. Runs 100% locally on your machine.
about: AI Society is a civilization simulation game where every character is driven by a local AI model.  Choose your mode:    In AI Town, build a society full of townsfolk who live their own lives.      In AI Game Studio, hire an AI dev team, run the company, and play the game they make.       AI TOWN   Create up to 25 unique characters and define who they are:    Set personality traits; how peaceful, hardworking, extroverted, generous, playful, or dominant they are    Give them hobbies like fishing, wood carving, or leatherworking    Write a freeform description to shape their worldview and backstory    Choose their appearance and gender    Your characters are fully autonomous. They will:    Find jobs and fill roles in the town's economy based on their personalities    Earn and spend money, manage hunger, and seek rest    Form relationships, some warm, some tense, based on their traits and interactions    Get married and have children to continue their legacy    Post thoughts, reactions, and confrontations on their own social media    Fight with characters they despise, and if things go badly, die permanently    Drop what they're doing to swarm the intruders when bandits raid the town    When a character dies, they're gone. Their job goes unfilled. Their relationships dissolve. They're remembered in the town cemetery, where others may visit their grave. With a revive token, they can be brought back to life.  Level up your town by going on adventures and reaching milestones:    Play 6 mini-games and fight through 5 tiered dungeons with your strongest characters    Win rare, epic, and exclusive legendary artifacts that give your characters special perks    March your whole population into battle against rival towns    Earn town XP for milestones like surviving your first bandit raid    Characters who die in a dungeon die for good    Control the town with your god powers:    Put thoughts in characters' heads    Force a confrontation or an encounter    Smite town resources or exile your characters    Heal characters before dungeon raids    Pick up characters and drop them anywhere on the map    Watch them react to your decisions on their social media       AI GAME STUDIO   Play a game made by a studio you run. Your team of AI employees designs it, builds it, markets it, and ships it, and every part of it comes out of their work and your decisions. No two studios make the same game.  The game your team makes:    A top-down pixel RPG with villages, dungeons, bosses, quests, shops, loot, levels, and gear    Every quest is completable and every dungeon is beatable    It keeps growing as your team keeps working, and you can go back in any time to see what's new    Run the company from a retro desktop:    A dev board, team page, the books, a marketing app, a store page, and a chat app your team gossips on    Walk around your pixel-art office, sit with people at lunch, and call meetings    Expand to a bigger office as the studio grows    Hire a small team and keep them happy:    Programmers, designers, artists, a marketer, an accountant    Each one has a personality, moods, loyalty, and opinions about you that they'll say to your face    Make them stay late and they remember it. Miss payroll and their mood and loyalty drop    Point them in a direction, in your own words:    Tell your team what kind of game you want and they take it from there. Your designer turns it into work, your programmers build it, your artist gives it a look    Watch tasks move across the board, see what failed and why, and make them try again    Call meetings where employees report in and pitch ideas. Accept one and it goes on the board    Ship it and face the market:    Launch on the in-world store in Early Access or at 1.0    Players buy it and leave honest reviews. A thin game gets "Mostly Negative" and you feel it in the numbers    Hire a marketer who runs campaigns on their own and asks for your sign-off on big spends    Cover rent and weekly payroll an

name: Arcana, Gas & Waterworks Inc.
lang: English**
short: Route magickal energy through a fantasy utility as a mid-level employee. Connect resources to consumers, manage complaints, and maintain the mana flow in this comedic puzzle-strategy-story game set in a mundane, magickal world. The benefits are not great, but neither is the pay. Welcome to the team!
about: Welcome to Arcana, Gas & Waterworks Inc.     "Keeping the mana flowing since 643 A.O."    You've just been hired at AG&W Inc, the municipal utility company responsible for delivering magical energy, gas, and water to every town, tower, dungeon, and dragon's lair in the region. Your job is to lay the ley lines, pipe the pipe networks, and route the resources to the right customers. Your placement is probationary, and you share a desk.  Nobody thanks you when things work, but everyone blames you when they don't.   ROUTE MAGICAL INFRASTRUCTURE     Connect sources to consumers across hex-grid maps    Manage 5 mana energy types: Arcana, Fire, Water, Earth, and Gas    Build relay stations, splitters, transformers, batteries, and filters    Watch your network come alive with glowing neon energy flows (then watch a dragon submit a three-page grievance about not having cold water)     SOLVE PUZZLES WITH CONSEQUENCES     Balance budgets while keeping customers satisfied    Handle escalating complaints from pixies, gnomes, dwarves, and dungeon lords    Discover energy interactions for better and mostly worse    Navigate 19 hand-crafted campaign scenarios across 6 career tiers     CLIMB THE CORPORATE LADDER     Start as a New Employee, rise to Chief of Reclamation    Unlock new components and abilities as you progress    Earn promotions by completing increasingly complex operations    Discover the dark secrets lurking in the company's past     EXPERIENCE RETRO-FUTURISTIC CHARM     VAX/VMS CRT terminal aesthetic with phosphor glow and scanlines    Classic OS-inspired desktop hub     WynnAmp 2.7.3 music player    Fantasy world corporate satire  with a mysterious start-up scandal     AMAZING INDIE MUSIC SOUNDTRACK     13 songs by 4 real life independent musicians:    Nobody and the NeckRomancers    Fire Ant Season     Backspin ZX    Harder Wins      Unlock new songs on almost every level     FEATURES     19 campaign scenarios with hand-crafted puzzles    Procedurally generated freelance operations for endless endgame replayability    23 Steam achievements    Soundtrack that slaps    Full keyboard rebinding    Supports accessible gaming settings     ALL PROCEEDS FROM THIS GAME WILL BE DONATED TO THE TREVOR PROJECT    100% of all income this game earns on Steam (or anywhere else) will be donated to The Trevor Project , a nonprofit dedicated to suicide prevention among LGBTQ+ youth. In their own words:   "The Trevor Project is the leading suicide prevention and crisis intervention nonprofit organization for LGBTQ+ young people. We provide information & support to LGBTQ+ young people 24/7, all year round."   If you are having thoughts of harming yourself or just need help working through a crisis, you can reach out 24/7 to The Trevor Project:  Text  START  to 678-678  Call 1-866-488-7386  TTY 1-866-803-3699  Online Chat   The team at AG&W Inc. want you to know that we love you and we're glad you're here. Scrollsworth even wrote a lengthy memo about how much he appreciates you being in our world. (He is requiring everyone to scroll to the bottom to acknowledge the message before they are permitted close the window.)      Arcana, Gas & Waterworks Inc. is a loving tribute to infrastructure games, 90s operating systems, and  corporate bureaucracy.

name: Fantasy Grounds - D&D Wayfinder's Guide to Eberron
lang: English
short: Explore Eberron with this playtest material featuring unique races, dragonmarks, and new magic items. A beautifully designed reference manual is included along with custom decals and 37 pieces of artwork. New content includes 4 races, 43 magic items, and a Quick Sharn Story template for adventures.
about: Wayfinder's Guide to Eberron  Important Note:  This is playtest material and should be considered  Early Access . Additional content and mechanics will be added after playtest feedback is received by Wizards of the Coast. There may be some delay in updating the Fantasy Grounds module after any new versions are released and provided to SmiteWorks. Eberron was born in 2002 when Wizards of the Coast launched a worldwide search for a new campaign setting.  Wayfinder's Guide to Eberron  brings the eponymous campaign setting to the fifth edition of  Dungeons & Dragons . This module has been converted from a 175 page book to give you everything you need to create an Eberron story or character, exploring the core themes of the setting and the rules to implement them in fifth edition. It includes an overview of Khorvaire and the fantastic city of Sharn, along with a host of background ideas and story hooks. Playtest material includes the unique races of Eberron, the mystical dragonmarks (including greater dragonmarks and aberrant dragonmarks), and new magic items; this is built upon a living document, and this content will evolve and be updated in response to feedback. name: Glyph Gambit Demo
lang: English
short: A turn-based tactical roguelite where you battle across grid-based arenas, destroy the enemy King before they destroy yours, and protect your Glyphs—lost if you fall, recoverable only by clearing the level where they dropped.
about: Glyph Gambit  is a turn-based tactical roguelite inspired by chess, Dark Souls, and grid-based dungeon crawlers. Each run challenges you to navigate dangerous tactical arenas where every move matters and every decision can end your journey. Your objective is clear:   Destroy the enemy King before they destroy yours.   You control multiple upgradable pieces on compact battle grids, facing distinct enemy factions with their own movement patterns and threats. Equip offensive  Edges , defensive  Shields , and powerful  Gems  and  Items  to shape your build and survive deeper into the gauntlet.  At the heart of the game are  Glyphs —the soul of your run. Glyphs empower your piece, unlock new abilities, and fuel long-term progression. But they are fragile. If you fall in battle, your Glyphs drop on that level. To reclaim them, you must return to that same encounter and clear it. Fail again before recovery, and those Glyphs are lost forever.   Tactical Combat on Compact Grids   Fight on small, focused encounter boards where positioning is everything. Predict enemy intent, manage danger zones, and outmaneuver rival Kings. Every run presents new tactical puzzles that reward smart planning and bold plays.   A Souls-Inspired Challenge Loop   Death resets the run—but permanent upgrades, unlocked items, and new Glyphs progressively expand your options. Each attempt pushes you further as you refine your strategy and piece loadout.   Distinct Enemy Factions & Bosses   Face Goblin raiders, Sage spellcasters, Usurpers, Plague creatures, Warlords, and ancient Tyrant bosses—each with unique attack shapes and movement patterns that challenge you to adapt and survive.   Build Your Piece With Permanent Items   Equip a wide range of upgrades including:     Edges  – Offensive stat boosts     Shields  – Defensive enhancements     Gems  – For upgrading edges and shields     Glyphs  – The soul of the game for leveling up and purchasing items     Permanent Items   - Items that can be used across all runs     Run Items    - Items that can be used for one run     Level Items  - Items that can be used for one level in a run     Consumables  - Items that are applied and consumed immediately     Designed for Controllers & Steam Deck   Featuring full controller support and clean UI navigation, Glyph Gambit plays naturally on both desktop and Steam Deck.   FEATURES     Turn-based tactical battles on compact grid arenas    Roguelite runs with permanent progression and unlocks    Core objective: destroy their King before they destroy yours    Glyphs that drop on death and can be lost forever    Dozens of Edges, Shields, and Gems to shape your build    Procedural encounters and branching run paths    Distinct factions with unique patterns and bosses    Souls-like atmosphere and challenge    Full controller support and Steam Deck compatible    Highly replayable with deep strategic choices
